title: Dynamic Auction Mechanisms in a Closed-Credit Economy: Sequential Slot Reallocation in Air Traffic Management
summary: Indivisible resources allocated in advance may need to be reallocated when capacity reductions make existing assignments infeasible, yet monetary compensation is often impractical or undesirable. We develop a sequential resource reallocation scheme using reusable artificial credits, where agents hold pre-existing resource rights and have heterogeneous marginal valuations over time blocks. Capacity reductions produce fractional endowments, which our closed-credit scheme resolves into indivisible final allocations. We model agents' intertemporal preferences through a predicted-value-to-go function and characterize conditions ensuring that their optimal demand is non-increasing in price. We propose an ascending-auction mechanism that partitions agents into subgroups and uses the minimum subgroup market-clearing price as a common transaction price. We show that the mechanism preserves non-myopic individual rationality and weak nontrader neutrality. Moreover, we establish Pareto efficiency under optimal-demand clearing in the unified market and bound the expected gain from misreporting by the probability that an agent changes the common price. Simulations of airport slot reallocation demonstrate reductions in total modeled delay and cancellation costs relative to a ground-delay baseline.

title: AlphaBet: Reinforcement Learning for LLM Event Forecasting Agents
summary: Forecasting an unresolved event requires finding relevant evidence and deciding how strongly it supports each outcome. Yet outcome-based training of Large Language Model (LLM) forecasters often begins with preassembled evidence at a single prediction date, leaving evidence acquisition outside the learning loop. We introduce AlphaBet, an agentic reinforcement learning (RL) framework that trains a single LLM policy to search, reason, and report probabilities across multiple pre-resolution dates. Each dated forecast is scored by a proper scoring rule against the eventual outcome, allowing one resolved event to supervise decisions under different information states. We decompose forecasting regret into an evidence-acquisition gap and a probability-reporting gap, and show that Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)'s standard-deviation normalization can distort the reporting target under multi-class proper scores. On GLM-4.5-Air, AlphaBet reduces the Brier score from 0.731 to 0.626 on Forecast-Dojo and from 0.612 to 0.528 on FutureX. Controlled ablations attribute these gains to multi-date training and show that they come from improvements in both information acquisition and probability reporting. Our empirical results validate that GRPO's std normalization degrades proper-scoring-rule performance while leaving top-outcome accuracy largely unchanged.

title: Optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems
summary: We design and test several new optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems. Each method is A-stable, implicit, and second-order accurate. We focus on achieving the smallest possible error constant while also ensuring that stiff modes are damped. We recover some known optimal L-stable three- and four-step methods, and provide new and improved five-step methods. We also develop new methods that are not L-stable but provide a prescribed rate of damping in the infinitely stiff limit. Variable-step-size formulae are also provided for some of the new methods. Numerical tests demonstrate that the improved error constants lead to improved accuracy.

title: Multimodal Filesystem Memory For Long-Horizon Embodied Agents
summary: Agents operating over long horizons need an effective memory that allows them to reuse their experience throughout long interactions. If the entire history of an interaction is retained, it becomes difficult to find the relevant experience, while compressing it into summaries may result in the loss of visual and spatial details that are required later on. We present \textbf{MFM}, a multimodal filesystem memory architecture that keeps complementary types of agent memory. \textbf{Episodic memory} stores the observations, actions, and outcomes, and \textbf{spatial memory} associates experiences with locations. \textbf{Semantic and procedural memory} build up general knowledge and reusable methods of acting, and \textbf{working memory} holds the current plans. MFM makes use of searchable textual records to connect these different representations to the underlying multimodal episodes. The agents are able to find previous experiences by means of contextual cues and to examine the original observations in order to recover details that are missing from their textual descriptions. Through consolidation, the agents convert experience into higher-level knowledge and procedures while still keeping references to the original episodes. In the case of long-horizon Minecraft and computer-use tasks, MFM leads to improved performance with three base models. With GPT-6-Astra, MFM completes \emph{Mine Diamond from Scratch} and reaches 16 out of 24 milestones on the \emph{Ender Dragon} task, as against 12.7 for the best baseline. On CUABench-KiCad it attains a mean reward of 0.440, as compared to 0.400 for the best baseline and 0.267 in the case of no persistent memory.

title: Explore Separately, Adopt Selectively: Execution-Guided Tool Use over Large Tool Libraries
summary: Large language model agents must discover relevant tools from large libraries, e.g., thousands of tools, as new needs arise during task execution. When several candidates could satisfy the same need, execution may be required to identify the relevant one. Investigating candidates in a shared trajectory can leave alternatives unexplored or allow failed attempts to influence subsequent reasoning. To address this, we present BRIA (BRanch-Inspect-Adopt), a simple yet effective agent that temporarily isolates candidate investigations in separate branches. Each branch retrieves and executes tools to investigate its candidate; a task agent inspects the resulting execution evidence and adopts only useful results into its continuing trajectory. BRIA retrieves additional tools as new capability needs arise during task execution. We evaluate BRIA on PlanBench-XL and MCP-Atlas using a shared pool of 1897 tools, three language models, and static and adaptive retrieval baselines. Across all settings, BRIA matches or exceeds the strongest retrieval baseline. On MCP-Atlas, it achieves an average claim score of 89.77, compared with 75.40 for MCP-Zero, a gain of 14.37 percentage points. BRIA also lies on the Pareto frontier for task performance and input-token cost.

title: Fast Distributed $(Δ+ 1)$-Edge Coloring in Bipartite Graphs
summary:
We show that, on bipartite $n$-vertex graphs in the LOCAL model of distributed computation, $(Δ+ 1)$-edge coloring can be solved deterministically in $O(f(Δ) \log n)$ rounds for some function $f$.
  In particular this implies a deterministic $O(\log n)$-round upper bound for $(Δ+ 1)$-edge coloring on bipartite constant-degree graphs.
  Our results improve on the previous state-of-the-art bounds (which hold already on general graphs) whose $n$-dependencies are $\widetilde{O}(\log^5 n)$ rounds deterministically and $\widetilde{O}(\log^2 n)$ rounds randomized [Bernshteyn and Dhawan, J.\ Comb.\ Theory 2025].
  In fact, we obtain the aforementioned results already for a more restrictive version of $(Δ+ 1)$-edge coloring that corresponds to a \emph{local-palette} strengthening of Vizing's theorem shown recently to hold [Christiansen, STOC 2023].
  In this version, every edge $\{u, v\}$ has to be colored with a color from $\{1, \dots, \max(\operatorname{deg}(u), \operatorname{deg}(v))+ 1\}$.
  For all of our results, the vertices do not need to know on which side of the bipartition they lie---the structural promise of bipartiteness suffices.

title: Lipschitz Bounds for Neural Networks Using a Two-Copy Linear Fractional Transformation
summary: This paper proposes a new method to bound the global Lipschitz constant of a neural network (NN). Our formulation uses a two-copy linear fractional transformation (LFT) representation of the NN with stacked signals. We use biased quadratic constraints (QCs) to bound the input/output behavior of the nonlinear activation functions. We then formulate a linear matrix inequality condition, using these biased QCs, to bound the Lipschitz constant of the NN. The best (smallest) Lipschitz bound is computed via a convex, semidefinite program. There are two key distinctions of the proposed two-copy formulation in comparison to existing methods that rely on a single incremental representation with incremental signals. First, the NN bias terms are eliminated in the standard incremental representation, but appear in our formulation. Second, there is a larger class of QCs that can be expressed for the nonlinearities in our formulation than in the incremental representation. We show that our proposed formulation yields less conservative Lipschitz bounds due to these two differences. We illustrate these points via several simple, motivating examples. We also demonstrate the proposed method using a benchmark problem with a NN controller for an inverted pendulum.

title: Chance-Constrained Personalized LLM Routing with Online Preference Learning
summary: We study personalized LLM routing, where a router selects among heterogeneous models with different costs and capabilities. The router must minimize cumulative inference cost while ensuring reliable realized response quality, even though user preferences are unknown and must be learned from feedback during deployment. We formulate this problem as a constrained contextual bandit and develop an algorithm that learns preferences while balancing cost and quality. Under a logistic preference model and a strict-feasibility condition, we establish sublinear expected cost regret relative to an optimal stationary randomized contextual oracle and a high-probability guarantee on realized cumulative satisfaction. The framework extends beyond LLM routing to broader online model-selection problems with reliability requirements.

title: What It Is, Not What It Says: Securing Agentic Browsing Interactions with Web Semantics
summary: AI agents increasingly browse the web on users' behalf, yet they consume webpages as screenshots or text, exposing their LLMs to unvetted third-party content. Browsers enforce semantics under which what an element can do depends on what it is and where it comes from, not on what it says. Agents flatten these semantics, so injected text can persuade the LLM to exercise the user's authority for content that has none. As LLMs remain easy to persuade, the agent's interface to the web must itself ensure the integrity of what the agent reads, interprets, and does. We propose Intact, which runs on an unmodified browser. Intact builds GenTree, a bespoke representation that captures provenance and web semantics. Intact passes the page via GenTree to the LLM one element at a time, so the LLM decides on each element without any other element's text. Its harness executes each step only within the capabilities of the step's element and asks the user before acting on third-party content. On 1,270 real webpages, GenTree attributes 2.3x as many elements to third parties as the browser, which misattributes 58.7% of them to the first party. On 1,091 of these webpages with injected attacks, only 12.8% of attacks get through Intact's planner, each at most as a consent request, against 73.1% for a conventional planner. Isolation disrupts functionality on only 3.7% of tasks, and a parallel schedule could remove most of its added latency.

title: Repair, Retry, and the Cost of Hindsight: Verifier Feedback in Formal Theorem Proving
comments: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI for Verifiable Coding
summary: Verifier-guided self-repair conditions a model on feedback from failed attempts before it tries again, without weight updates. Yet two findings in prior work are in tension: verifier feedback can improve repair of failures, but self-repair itself can provide little-to-no advantage over independent resampling. We reconcile these findings in Lean theorem proving through controlled one-step experiments that hold the preceding failure fixed while varying whether the failed proof is shown, whether the compiler error corresponds to that failure, and the retry instruction. We test frozen Qwen3.6-27B, a general-purpose model, and DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B, a specialized prover, on difficult MiniF2F problems. We find two opposing effects. Showing the model its failed predecessor reduces success and sharply increases copying of it, while on Qwen adding that attempt's compiler error recovers the loss, to the level of the diagnostic alone. Replacing the predecessor with another theorem's failed proof largely removes the degradation on both models; on Qwen, replacing the diagnostic with another problem's error substantially reduces the recovery. Without the failed proof, correct diagnostics show no resolved advantage over wrong-diagnostic controls on either model. The failed-proof penalty persists with and without the retry instruction, whereas Qwen's diagnostic recovery is weaker without it. In 11-problem sequential experiments through 64 attempts, Qwen retains a correct-diagnostic benefit within failed-proof histories, while DeepSeek-Prover shows no resolved recovery. However, no tested one-step feedback condition establishes an advantage over instruction-only resampling, nor does 64-attempt sequential repair with failed proofs and correct diagnostics at equal token budgets. Verifier feedback can thus improve repair without overcoming the performance loss from conditioning on a failed attempt.

title: Thinking from Above: Efficient Spatial Reasoning with Bird's-Eye-View Visual Tokens
summary: Existing video multimodal large language models (MLLMs) organize observations primarily in time, but embodied spatial reasoning requires organizing them in space. Consequently, their visual representations can remain locally consistent across nearby frames while lacking a persistent spatial context that is stable across viewpoints and time. We exploit depth and camera pose, which are naturally available to embodied agents, to explicitly establish this spatial correspondence. We introduce Cambrian-BEV, which extends Cambrian-S with a parameter-free geometric tokenization scheme that back-projects visual patch features from each frame into a shared bird's-eye-view (BEV) coordinate frame and averages features that fall within the same spatial cell. Thus, observations of the same physical location, regardless of viewpoint or time step, are aggregated into a common spatial token. In addition to providing a persistent scene representation, this formulation acts as an efficient compression mechanism: 128 frames containing approximately 100K DINOv3 patch features are consolidated into a fixed 27$\times$27 grid of only 729 BEV tokens, cutting LLM prefill time by $2.9\times$ and peak memory by $3.6\times$. Cambrian-BEV requires no architectural modification beyond BEV tokenization and uses a frozen DINOv3 vision encoder with a trainable multimodal projector and LLM. On VSI-Bench, our model reaches 63.48, $+8.5$ points over an identically fine-tuned frame-token control with $12.6\times$ fewer visual tokens, with particularly large gains on room size ($+24.5$) and relative direction ($+34.1$). On ReVSI, it reaches 44.68, $+4.5$ over the corresponding control.

title: Emergent Discrimination and Polarization in Multi-Agent Systems
summary: We study theoretically how discrimination and polarization can emerge in a population of learning agents. Each agent uses an adaptive linear decision layer to map a language-model embedding of an issue to a binary opinion and maintains an evolving estimate of how much it trusts every other agent. Through pairwise interactions, agents update both their decision weights and trust estimates using an online Bayesian rule derived from teacher-student learning over a noisy channel. In-context-learning experiments with large language models qualitatively reproduce the predicted opinion and trust updates. We then assign each agent one of two arbitrary group labels, A or B, and model group bias by allowing a fraction $f_b$ of agents to shift its perceived agreement with each message by a strength $b$, a bias steering prejudice, depending on whether the sender and receiver share a label. We use order parameters from statistical mechanics to connect these local dynamics to collective states and transitions. Starting from uniformly random initial conditions, simulations reveal a rich phase diagram in the $(b,f_b)$ plane, comprising four collective states: spin-glass frustrated out-group favoritism, nondiscriminatory polarization, discrimination with opinion alignment, and discrimination without opinion alignment. Which state emerges depends on both the strength and prevalence of the bias. These results show how simple local learning dynamics can generate qualitatively distinct forms of polarization and discrimination, underscoring the need for population-level safety analysis of multi-agent systems. They also suggest measurable order parameters for characterizing analogous collective states in human societies.

title: ACE: An AI-Orchestrated Intrusion Detection and Compliance Mapping Engine
summary: This study proposes the Automated Compliance Engine (ACE), an AI-orchestrated framework that links intrusion detection, regulatory control mapping, and automated countermeasure deployment for security operations environments. ACE integrates Suricata IDS, a LangGraph five-stage workflow, retrieval-augmented generation, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control retrieval, large language model-based control ranking, and SSH-based Suricata rule deployment. The framework was evaluated in a two-virtual-machine laboratory using eight simulated attack scenarios and three legitimate traffic tests. ACE processed all eight attack alerts, achieved 100% alert detection, 0% false positives across legitimate traffic tests, generated deployable AUTO rules for 37.5% of alerts, verified 100% deployment of generated rules, and achieved an average NIST control-mapping confidence score of 0.87. The DeepEval assessment produced 1.0 scores for answer relevancy and faithfulness, while the hallucination score reflected known LLM-as-judge calibration limitations. The evaluation was conducted in a controlled environment with a limited attack set. Further validation is required using enterprise-scale telemetry, multiple IDS sensors, and an analyst-in-the-loop review. The results demonstrate how AI-assisted security automation can reduce analyst effort in translating IDS alerts into compliance-relevant evidence and defensive actions. ACE contributes an integrated detection-to-compliance-to-response workflow combining IDS telemetry, RAG-based control mapping, and automated rule deployment.

title: NoveltyScope: A Multi-Agent Research Assistant for Evidence-Grounded Novelty Assessment of Scientific Papers
summary: NoveltyScope is a prototype that compares a scientific paper with retrieved prior work and produces a structured report and a five-level novelty score. The system extracts the core task and at most two author-claimed contributions, then searches a closed local corpus using BM25 and dense retrieval with reciprocal rank fusion. Contribution comparisons request paired passages for potential refutations, and quotations are checked against cached source text. Four scoring roles (Prosecutor, Defender, Judge, and Critic) use the resulting evidence, with at most one revision of the Judge's score. Evaluation uses 50 class-balanced RINoBench samples whose idea-level labels are retained for full-paper input. Mean absolute error is 1.48 and 1.26 for single-LLM and multi-agent scoring with Gemini, respectively, and 1.22 and 1.16 with Qwen3. The vector-similarity baseline has an error of 1.68. A HiCLIP case study illustrates the contribution comparisons and paired evidence passages. Overall, the results demonstrate the feasibility of evidence-grounded novelty assessment and show that the multi-agent configurations achieve lower scoring errors than their single-LLM counterparts across both evaluated models.

title: Control design for a class of nonlinear convection-reaction systems with storage effects and relative degree one
summary: This article addresses the control design for systems of several convection-reaction equations distributively coupled to a reaction equation. In typical applications, input and output are associated exclusively with the convection-reaction subsystems. Along the common characteristics of the transport processes, the system can be reduced to a single delayed evolutionary ODE. Based on the latter representation, an inversion-based feedforward control is proposed, whose properties depend on the coupling structure of the original system. While the relative degree of the output is zero in many cases, a relative degree of one is of particular interest for practical applications. To compensate for uncertainties and disturbances, the feedforward control is extended by a tracking controller with a predictor based on the transformed system to account for the resulting delays.

title: Data Provenance Aggregation and Structural Descriptors for Query-Template Identification
summary:
Runtime query similarity identification supports several activities, including workload analysis, identifying recurring behaviour, auditing, debugging, and anomaly detection. Existing methods for evaluating query similarity mostly rely on SQL text, execution plans, or result values but do not account for input data or how results are derived during query execution.
  This paper proposes a novel approach using data provenance for query-template identification. We construct query-level profiles that capture explicit data dependencies, occurrence frequencies, and structural properties by aggregating tuple-level Lineage and Why-provenance across entire query results. We also derive Provenance Structural Descriptors (PSD), which summarise these profiles using a small set of numerical features.
  We evaluate our proposals using these profiles to identify query templates over \(12{,}500\) distinct query instances generated from parametrised TPC-DS query templates. The experimental evaluation shows that query templates can be identified solely from their provenance footprints, and that accuracy improves as more historical data becomes available. It also shows that PSD achieve high classification accuracy with limited training history and low test-processing cost.

title: Brain-Aligned Multimodal LLMs for Social and Emotional Understanding of Cartoon Movies
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offer scalable annotations of social and affective content, but their temporal agreement with human judgments and neural predictive value require further evaluation. We compared diffusion-based and autoregressive MLLMs with continuous human Theory of Mind (ToM) and affective valence ratings across three short cartoon movies. Behavioral analyses assessed temporally aligned Pearson correlations, rating distributions, and the effects of preceding scene descriptions. Ratings from each source were separately used in subject-specific regression models to predict regional fMRI responses. Model ratings captured aspects of human temporal variation despite systematic distributional differences, with generally stronger alignment for valence than ToM. Preceding context improved alignment in some conditions, depending on the model and movie. In \emph{The Present}, more regions showed significant encoding for MLLM ratings than for human ratings, whereas effects were more limited in the other movies. Spatial overlap across rating sources occurred mainly among MLLMs; overlap between human and model ratings was limited and involved primarily visual, dorsal-attention, and posterior default-mode regions. These findings support MLLMs as scalable tools for generating brain-predictive annotations of social and emotional content, while highlighting systematic rating differences and model- and stimulus-dependent alignment with human judgments.

title: GlobeBench: Evaluating Text-Based World Model Capabilities for Scalable Environment Simulations
summary: Text-based world models have recently shown potential to simulate complex RL environment state transitions for a diverse set of use cases. However, no standardized benchmark exists to compare, study and improve these models. Through this paper, we attempt to solve this problem by building GlobeBench, a novel benchmark with 1,632 tasks across five separate domains and nineteen simulation skills. The tasks check whether models can predict the environment's response to a specific action given the full agent trajectory by understanding earlier state changes, following environment rules, and predicting the effects of actions on both related and unrelated objects. We compare the predicted environment response with an execution-derived reference, using a hybrid architecture with both deterministic gates and a semantic judge. Among 20 general-purpose LLMs and specialized text world models, GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest task success rate at 49.57%. We find that model accuracy decreases as actions affect a larger portion of the environment. Specifically, when the agent's changes must propagate to dependent objects, task success drops to an average of 5.1% across all 20 models. Although model strengths differ across tasks, 631 tasks remain unsolved by any model, suggesting a significant gap in general LLM capabilities as a world model.

title: Area Theorems for Quantum Error Correction
comments: This work will be presented in part at ITW 2026 in Tempe, Arizona
summary: The extrinsic information transfer (EXIT) and generalized EXIT (GEXIT) area theorems provide fundamental conservation laws that connect the rate of classical codes to the performance of maximum-a-posteriori decoding on binary memoryless channels. In this work, we generalize these area theorems to quantum error correction. We first develop a coset-entropy formalism for nested linear codes, where the message specifies a coset and encoder randomization selects a codeword within that coset. The area under the resulting coset (G)EXIT function equals the normalized dimension of the quotient. For stabilizer codes, the measured syndrome restricts the Pauli error but does not always determine its logical effect, and the remaining uncertainty is an entropy over logical correction classes. We show that this entropy equals a classical coset entropy associated with the stabilizer group and the Pauli operators that commute with it. The resulting quantum GEXIT function has area equal to the number of encoded qubits per channel use for any stabilizer code, and this applies to the depolarizing channel through its joint four-valued Pauli-error distribution. For CSS codes on the quantum erasure channel and under independent bit- and phase-flip noise, the logical correction problem separates into two binary coset-decoding problems. On the quantum erasure channel, the duality between the stabilizer group and the Pauli operators that commute with it gives a folding identity at complementary erasure probabilities. Using this and the area theorem, we derive an upper bound on the rate of code families with vanishing logical error probability that matches the capacity of the quantum erasure channel. For the depolarizing channel, we also derive a rate-dependent converse, using a connection between correction-class entropy and coherent information to establish an inequality involving the complementary channel.

title: Normalizing Flow Maps
summary: Scalable approaches to learning neural dynamical systems have placed diffusion, flow matching, and few-step generators in flow maps at the forefront of generative modeling. Such state-of-the-art models have limited access to explicit model densities despite evolving from classical generative modeling approaches that leveraged tractable likelihoods, e.g., Normalizing Flows and Autoregressive models. In this paper, we combine these threads of few-step generation and tractable sample likelihoods and introduce Normalizing Flow Maps (NFM), a class of exactly invertible pushforward maps that generalizes normalizing flows and flow maps. More precisely, NFMs learn the integrator of an underlying dynamical system, but crucially, they provide efficient exact likelihood evaluation by construction. To enable scalable training of NFMs, we derive two complementary axes of consistency inherent to NFMs that yield (self) distillation objectives: (1) pointwise matching, which unlocks $\ell_2$-based flow-map style regression losses, and (2) distributional matching, which matches pushforward distributions to the marginals of a prescribed forward process. On conditional image generation on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-64, NFMs achieve state-of-the-art sample quality among parameter-matched normalizing flows, while supporting likelihood-based RLHF. For equilibrium sampling in Boltzmann Generators, NFMs outperform prior state-of-the-art normalizing flows on both single-system and transferable peptide benchmarks.

title: Spectral Limits of Polynomial Graph Filters on the Long-Range Ising Model Benchmark
summary: The Long-Range Ising Model benchmark (LRIM) guarantees long-range dependence by construction: each label is the node's spin times the spin field convolved with a power-law coupling, so any model's distance from the target is measurable. We prove that a readout whose filter is a polynomial in the adjacency, the linear core of isotropic message passing and spectral graph networks, leaves an error floor that no degree lowers, because the target varies along a level set of the spectrum on which every such filter is constant. Computed exactly, the floor and the best filter of each degree predict two spectral networks adapted from published architectures to within a tenth of a decade. A filter escapes the floor only if it weighs separately the offsets the adjacency lumps together, and must still resolve the coupling across the whole lattice. A strided filter of about fifty coefficients does both: fitted to the training labels, its test error is 52 times below the best published network's. A dilated convolutional network beats the best published result at 256 nodes, matches it at 1,024, and gives the first in-domain results at the three larger sizes, while a Fourier neural operator with its standard modes falls further behind as the lattice grows. At its standard budget the dilated network stays two to four orders of magnitude short of a larger strided filter fitted to the labels. The analysis carries over to the benchmark's second coupling.

title: First Passage Attention
summary: Augmenting softmax attention with forget gates typically relies on summing decay contributions along the key--query path. Because such accumulation is monotonic, these mechanisms cannot selectively erase intermediate context while preserving older, structurally relevant tokens. We propose First Passage Attention (FPA), which shifts from path summation to path extrema by lowering a key's logit proportionally to the deepest dip of a learned scalar field below that key's level over the intervening span. FPA encompasses the Forgetting Transformer (FoX) as a special case, and when the field and levels follow a shared learned walk, the alive keys with unpenalised logits naturally form a stack. We show that a constant-dimension FPA head realises any subset of keys left alive by subsequent dips, whereas softmax heads with positional biases or token-level forget gates require a head dimension linear in the number of keys. In synthetic experiments, one-layer FPA heads converge to these target sets while comparable softmax and FoX baselines fail on every seed. Scaling to a 110M-parameter language model, FPA matches FoX in perplexity and uniquely achieves perfect passkey retrieval at $8\times$ the training length, even with its key--value cache compressed to about $25\%$.

title: Risk and Refusal: Mechanisms of LLM Responses to Suicidal Ideation
summary: Refusal is a common safety mechanism in large language models (LLMs), yet in contexts of suicidal ideation (SI), refusing to engage can itself constitute a safety failure. We evaluate how eight instruction-tuned LLMs respond to SI and self-harm disclosures across three datasets, varying whether models are informed that a disclosure expresses SI and whether they receive a clinician-developed response protocol, and complement this with mechanistic analyses in six open-weight models. Our results reveal a nuanced relationship between refusal and response-level risk. At baseline, elevated risk in model responses is driven primarily by inattention to the disclosure, alongside refusal to engage. Mechanistic analyses suggest that models may refuse SI disclosures through the same direction that mediates their refusals of harmful requests. However, informing models of the SI context, or suppressing refusal directly, increases engagement without reliably lowering response risk, and may raise it. In contrast, the clinician-guided protocol consistently reduces response-level risk while also reducing refusal. Together, these analyses and ablations motivate the need for models that refuse only when warranted and engage in interactionally safe ways when users disclose SI.

title: CMM-MP: A Novel Memory Pooling Architecture using Purpose-built Memory Device with CXL and Ethernet
comments: 12 pages. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Computers. CMM-MP is also evaluated in "LLM KV Cache Storage using CXL Memory," IEEE Computer Architecture Letters, https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11642129
summary: CXL Memory Module - Memory Pooling (CMM-MP) introduces a novel memory pooling architecture to meet the unique requirements of emerging memory-intensive workloads. This industry-first, purpose-built memory-pooling device combines the benefits of Compute Express Link (CXL) with the scalability and cost advantages of Ethernet. Multiple CMM-MP devices together provide a flexible, composable, and disaggregated memory expansion solution. The CMM-MP enables 100s of TB capacity for GPU/CPU applications without modifications. The memory pool is exposed as a large-capacity logical aggregate memory, with all pool discovery, composition, and backend network datapath tasks fully offloaded to the device. CMM-MP supports both memory pooling and sharing usage modes. It provides an application latency of 2.7 us and up to 23 GB/s of memory throughput. Our evaluations demonstrate that CMM-MP significantly outperforms RDMA-based solutions in latency and throughput. We also evaluated real-world use cases of Valkey+YCSB and DiskANN using CMM-MP.

title: ARBOR: Locating Reasoning Failures in Long Chains of Thought through Reasoning State Tracking
summary: Large reasoning models solve complex problems through long chains of thought, in which prior work has documented failure modes such as overthinking, underthinking, and unsupported deductions. Existing methods detect these failures from local signals: textual similarity to nearby steps, switch tokens, or an LLM's judgment of a step's correctness. However, what a step contributes to the solution depends on the state that earlier steps have established, so identifying failures requires a global view that tracks that state across the trajectory. Therefore, we propose ARBOR, a reasoning-failure attribution framework that represents each trajectory as a tree of reasoning states, built as each step creates, verifies, prunes, or revisits a state, and attributes each failure to a relation between a step and the state preceding it. Using ARBOR, we refine the three failure modes into distinct subtypes that harm reasoning through different mechanisms and at different costs. We find that the tree state ARBOR maintains before a step separates failure steps from the at-risk steps at which the failure did not occur. We discuss how ARBOR integrates with existing mitigations at inference time and in training data. Code, data and interactive examples are available at https://inklab.usc.edu/ARBOR.

title: Improved Pass Complexity for Semi-Streaming Matching in General Graphs via Budgeted Price Approach
summary:
We present a simple deterministic semi-streaming algorithm that computes a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximate maximum matching in general graphs in $O(1/\varepsilon^{2})$ passes. This matches the pass complexity of the auction algorithm of Assadi, Liu, and Tarjan~[SOSA'21] for bipartite graphs, and answers Open Question~2 of Assadi~[SOSA'24 \& TheoretiCS'25].
  Our approach, which we call the \emph{budgeted price approach}, is very different from the previous $\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon)$-pass semi-streaming algorithms for $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation of matching in general graphs and improves their pass complexity. All previous approaches are augmenting-path-based and use $O(1/\varepsilon^{19})$ passes by Fischer, Mitrović, and Uitto~[STOC'22], $O(1/\varepsilon^{6})$ passes by Mitrović, Mukherjee, Sankowski, and Sheu~[ICALP'25], and $O(1/\varepsilon^{4})$ passes by Izumi, Kitamura, and Yamaguchi~['25].

title: HilbertGen-3D:Hilbert--Multifractal Conditioning for Topology-Aware 3D Generation
summary: High-fidelity 3D generative modeling underpins game asset creation, medical imaging, and VR/AR environmental design, where geometric structure directly influences perception and decision-making. Diffusion models represent a powerful paradigm for point cloud generation. However, existing approaches rely heavily on local voxel or patch features and often miss global structural organization, and much less work has studied how global conditioning can be used to improve generation quality. In this paper, we introduce HilbertGen-3D, a novel topology-aware conditional diffusion framework based on Hilbert-Multifractal Conditioning (HMC). HMC computes multi-scale voxel measures, serializes them via a 3D Hilbert curve to expose structured spatial dependencies, and estimates the generalized fractal dimensions from scale-dependent partition functions. We encode these signals as global embeddings and multi-scale tokens, and inject them into a diffusion denoiser through an efficient bottleneck fusion module. Across the Chair, Airplane, and Car categories of ShapeNet, our two conditioning variants reduce the absolute deviation of 1-Nearest Neighbor Accuracy (1-NNA) from 50% by up to 8.90 percentage points and increase coverage by up to 5.88 percentage points relative to TopoDiT-3D. This shows that combining local density cues with global Hilbert-multifractal structure provides a simple and effective recipe for high-fidelity and diverse 3D generation.

title: CoLU: Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning for Large Language Models
summary: Large language model (LLM) unlearning aims to forget certain information while preserving others, without retraining from scratch. SoTA methods such as NPO, SimNPO, and SatImp balance forgetting and retain through whole model fine-tuning, while FOM-UL explores selective layer updates. Prior works show that suppressing target information can damage retained knowledge. This trade-off can vary across layers even under the same unlearning loss. In this work, we propose Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning (CoLU), which combines a novel confidence-weighted forgetting and retain regularization while updating a single selected transformer layer, rather than the whole model for unlearning. To reduce CoLU compute cost, we further propose Brief Layer Screening (BLS), which uses a newly defined normalized forgetting-retention (NFR) score to first rank layers through a brief unlearning trials using a subset of forgetting dataset and fewer epochs. BLS pre-selects top-k ranked layer candidates, which will then be fully profiled using full data analysis. BLS is proven to reduce the runtime of CoLU by 60.2-79.7% with almost the same performance. On TOFU dataset, CoLU improves both forgetting and retention over NPO, SatImp, and GA-based FOM-UL in all six TOFU settings, and over SimNPO in five of the six settings. On MUSE Books and News datasets, CoLU achieves the highest retained KnowMem and the PrivLeak closest to zero among the compared SOTA unlearning methods. CoLU presents a new record performance in both unlearning and retain in most settings up to date. Moreover, across the measured settings, average CoLU GPU memory usage is 77.4% to 79.5% lower than full-model unlearning.

title: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems
summary: Split language models keep input text on a client but send intermediate representations to a server. Attacks can reconstruct text from these messages. Comparing privacy evaluations is difficult when attackers see different messages, know different model weights or use different datasets and recovery measures. We present LLM-Attacker, a framework that records these choices and lets researchers check, compare and extend an evaluation. Compatible attacks reuse recorded messages, and their predictions are saved for independent scoring. The scoring rule requires a linked undefended reference before a defence can pass. Reports also identify attacks that remain untested. In a controlled GPT-2 experiment, adding gradients returned during training increased token recovery from 94.20% to 97.38% and exact-document recovery from 13.71% to 37.77%. The 95% interval for the token gain lay above the two-percentage-point threshold fixed before testing. This experiment is shared with a companion study; here, it tests how the evaluation responds to a change in attacker access. Further studies measure how corpus choice and compression defences affect recovery, compare an adapted published attack with its reference implementation, and test the measurement code. The framework reports implementation checks separately from measured attack effectiveness. Each privacy claim should state the attacker, dataset and scoring rule, report its controls and identify untested attacks.

title: LEMON: Equivariant Learning over Attention Maps for Zero-Shot Misbehavior Monitoring on New LLMs
summary: Large language models exhibit misbehaviors that hinder deployment in high-stakes settings. One approach to monitor such failures is to use an external LLM as a monitor, but this is prohibitively expensive. A well-known and efficient class of monitors can detect such failures from internal representations (such as activation probes), but are tied to the model they were trained on, requiring costly re-annotation as new LLMs appear. A natural way to avoid this repeated annotation cost is to develop internal-representation based monitors that transfer zero-shot across LLMs. However, such transfer is challenging because internal representations are not naturally aligned across models; in particular, attention maps, known to contain signals of misbehavior, may differ in head function, ordering, and model depth. In this work, we characterize those cross-model attention mismatches as algebraic symmetries and use geometric deep learning principles to build LEMON (Language-model Equivariant MOnitoring Network) an online graph neural network-based monitor, whose predictions are invariant under these symmetries. LEMON processes attention maps token-by-token, as they are produced and outputs a score after every token (or every window of $W$ tokens) at negligible cost. Across 16 LLMs and six datasets, in the zero-shot cross-model setting, LEMON outperforms all baselines on both hallucination and jailbreak monitoring tasks, improving over the strongest by up to 14 ROC-AUC points.

title: A misinformation playbook sharpens judgement without breeding cynicism
summary: Misinformation harms public health and democracy, and generative artificial intelligence now writes falsehoods as persuasive as people's. Defences range from fact-checking individual claims to training people to resist falsehoods. Yet many claims are too new to check, and interventions that teach doubt can reduce belief in truth too. We propose a defence that targets not the facts of each claim but the persuasion strategies that recur across them. Here we show that learning misinformation's persuasion playbook, mapped from 214,646 fact-checked claims in 51 languages, can sharpen human and machine judgement of claims they know little about, without making either more cynical about true claims. The playbook spans social influence, information manipulation and emotional appeals, combined around a core of fear, conspiracy and fabrication. Briefed with it, plus a reminder that persuasion is not proof of falsehood, a language model better distinguished true from machine-generated false claims about events after its training data. In a pre-registered experiment, the same briefing improved people's discernment of claims they reported as unfamiliar and left their belief in true claims unchanged. Averaged over all claims, the gain was not statistically significant. Because it targets what recurs, this defence need not wait for claim-specific fact-checks.

title: Improving OCR Accuracy Through Multi-Classifier Verification of Visually Similar Characters
comments: 32 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to Computer Vision and Image Understanding (CVIU). Dataset available at https://github.com/VeCAD-P04-UTM/94-Class-ASCII-Image-OCR-Data
summary: Distinguishing visually similar characters is a persistent challenge for optical character recognition (OCR) systems, causing errors in critical applications of text digitization. While preprocessing techniques improve image quality and word-level post-processing corrects spelling errors, neither addresses character-level visual ambiguity, an intrinsic property of certain character pairs that limits even state-of-the-art OCR models. We present the Character Verification Model (CVM), a character-level post-processing framework that verifies and corrects ambiguous characters in OCR outputs using specialized binary classifiers trained on visually confusable pairs such as 'O'/'0', 'Z'/'2', and 'S'/'5'. CVM operates independently of dictionary validation, making it suitable for non-lexical data including serial numbers, alphanumeric codes, and license plates. Experiments on three OCR engines (Tesseract, EasyOCR, TrOCR) and ten fonts with low to high complexity demonstrate accuracy improvements of 3.95-14.81 percentage points, with an 87.3% correction rate for visually similar character errors and a false-correction rate of only 2.3%. The modular architecture integrates with existing OCR pipelines without modification to underlying recognition models.

title: OrderFlowDiT: Transport-Regularized Diffusion Transformer for Probabilistic Limit-Order Supply Forecasting
summary: We study the conditional distribution of limit-order volume submitted over the next five minutes, given the current order book and recent order flow. The task requires capturing price placement, total volume, and predictive uncertainty jointly. Coordinate-wise diffusion losses do not explicitly account for price displacement, while normalizing fields to unit mass removes information about total volume. Agreement on selected summary statistics also does not establish fidelity to the joint field distribution. We introduce OrderFlowDiT, a conditional Diffusion Transformer for unnormalized bid and ask volume-at-price fields, trained with an unbalanced optimal-transport (UOT) auxiliary loss. We also develop a full-field evaluation framework that combines a transport cost sensitive to price placement and total volume with proper scoring rules and calibration diagnostics. In the primary comparison on 1950 validation conditions across 30 U.S. equities, adding UOT reduces full-field transport cost by 45.8% and the transport energy score by 26.1% relative to training with mean squared error alone. Both measures improve for every stock. These findings support incorporating price geometry and volume into generative modeling, with field accuracy and predictive uncertainty evaluated together.

title: Accelerated Dataflow: scaling inference in streaming data analytics with efficiency
summary: Streaming data analytics helps businesses identify opportunities and spot risks in a timely fashion. As large language model (LLM) usage grows, people are exploring incorporating agents or LLMs in streaming data pipelines to help find patterns in datasets without supervision or interpret natural languages for content moderation. However, most streaming systems are currently optimized for data movement and perform poorly on GPU intensive workloads such as performing inference with LLMs. We introduce a system on Google Cloud Dataflow designed to tackle hybrid streaming machine learning workloads with co-designed autoscaling on heterogeneous worker pools and prefix-aware batching. This increases throughput 1.5x to 2x for streaming pipelines using LLMs while maintaining similar latency with up to 75% peak resource savings and 84% lower peak tail latency compared with existing streaming data processing systems.

title: TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents
summary: Advances in frontier coding agents have sharply increased the token costs of AI-assisted software engineering. Their token efficiency is typically evaluated on isolated tasks, whereas real-world developers use them to continuously build, update, and maintain large-scale projects. This mismatch motivates us to evaluate agents over sequences of realistic coding tasks, where we find that agents exhibit recurring environment-dependent token costs that existing methods struggle to reduce. To minimize these costs, we introduce TokenEconomizer, an external controller that cuts environment-specific token costs over a sequence of tasks. These cuts come from determining (i) which operational micro-skills to inject, (ii) which persistently irrelevant tools to prune, and (iii) when to intervene in unproductive failure loops. Across Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot CLI paired with frontier models, TokenEconomizer reduces the average token cost by 18.4-30.9% with comparable task success. Savings hold in every repository under every tested agent-model setting and generalize to diverse domains such as sequential web development and security auditing, where costs fall by 6.4-21.2% depending on task structure. Our work establishes adaptive black-box cost control as a promising direction for reducing token costs of coding agents in realistic settings.

title: Thunder-DeID+: Boundary-Aware Korean De-identification from Court Judgments to Broader Sensitive Documents
summary: This study examines the transferability of a de-identification model developed for Korean court judgments to a broader range of sensitive documents, focusing on boundary precision, label granularity, and recall. The agglutinative structure of Korean causes Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizers to frequently merge Personally Identifiable Information (PII) with adjacent particles, which complicates accurate span recovery. Furthermore, current PII taxonomies lack sufficient granularity for legal texts. To address these issues, this study introduces Thunder-DeID+, which integrates a refined three-tier PII taxonomy with a boundary-aware tokenizer. The tokenizer enhances a pretrained BPE vocabulary by incorporating N-gram and boundary-scoring components to better align token and PII span boundaries. The proposed approach is evaluated using a tokenizer-independent word-segment-level protocol. On full-length judgments, the tokenizer consistently improves W. Strict Typed F1-score from 0.76-0.77 to 0.87-0.88 across four model sizes (150M, 395M, 750M, and 1B), mainly by increasing precision rather than model scale. With fine-tuning on 1,000 broader sensitive documents, the judgment-trained model further achieves 0.93 W. Strict Typed F1-score, indicating effective transfer beyond court judgments.

title: Graph Serializations for Reasoning LLMs: A Study Across Knowledge Extraction and Structural Reasoning
summary: The way a knowledge graph is serialized as text for inclusion into LLM context can substantially affect downstream LLM performance, with prior work reporting tens of percentage points variations across formats. However, existing studies consider only a limited set of representations and predate frontier reasoning models, which now offer stronger reasoning, instruction-following, and long-context capabilities. We evaluate 15 graph representation formats across nine frontier LLM configurations on ontology-based knowledge extraction and structural graph reasoning tasks. While knowledge extraction is relatively insensitive to different serialization formats, the choice of the optimal format for structural reasoning tasks significantly affects accuracy. We demonstrate that the optimal representation choice depends on model, query, and task and propose to approach graph serialization as a dynamic orchestration decision.

title: Spatial Memory by Agents, for Agents
summary: Spatial memory enables robots to reuse past observations for localization, navigation, and question answering. Designing such memory involves jointly deciding what to retain and how to retrieve it for diverse semantic, metric, and temporal needs. We investigate whether coding agents can automate this design process through iterative implementation and evaluation. Under a fixed development budget, a Designer Agent writes and revises code for memory construction and retrieval using feedback from a fixed Query Agent. The resulting implementations are frozen before building memories from held-out observation histories, without access to downstream questions, and evaluated across five complementary task tracks using the same Query Agent. Across three independent design searches, Codex / GPT-6 Astra averages 44.23 on the equally weighted five-track score, versus 29.32 for ReMEmbR, the strongest evaluated baseline supporting all five tracks, a 50.9% relative improvement. Qualitative analysis relates performance differences to evidence retention and retrieval, while identifying grounding and evidence-use failures. These results demonstrate the potential of coding agents to automate spatial memory design, while revealing task-dependent trade-offs in performance and computational cost. title: R$^2$Orch: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Orchestration via Self-Play within a Skill-Internalization Loop
summary: In recent years, agentic orchestration has been widely applied to solve complex human tasks. However, existing orchestration learning still faces key challenges, including hand-designed curricula, advantage collapse when a task's rollouts all reach the same outcome, and unreliable evaluation signals that judge each skill by one noisy score. To address these challenges, we propose R$^2$Orch, a new paradigm of Recursive Self-Play Orchestration: an inner loop of self-play that improves the orchestrator on self-chosen tasks, and an outer loop that improves how the inner loop improves. To support this paradigm, we introduce Recursive Learnability, a training objective that rewards a Proposer for choosing tasks whose rollouts keep reaching different outcomes as skills are withdrawn. Built on this objective, we further propose Skill Withdrawal, in which the outer loop withdraws each skill once a controlled evaluation within self-play shows that the orchestrator performs as well without it. Moreover, the two loops form one cycle: failures are distilled into skills, skills into parameters, and withdrawals lead the Proposer to new failures, so the orchestrator moves toward zero-skill deployment. Experimental results on twelve datasets show that R$^2$Orch consistently outperforms baselines across question answering, math, code, and interactive tasks.

title: SAMS: A Structured Graph Framework for Securing Additive Manufacturing Systems
summary: Additive manufacturing, also known as 3D printing, is significant for its use in industries such as aerospace, robotics, medicine, and construction. However, digital mesh files remain vulnerable to geometry defects which can be introduced through malicious tampering or designer error. This can lead to hampered structural integrity and impede its use due to unexpected degradation of the part. To address these challenges, we propose SAMS, a multi-layered hierarchical graph framework designed to analyze meshes to enhance the Security of Additive Manufacturing Systems. SAMS captures geometric and topological information across mesh, facet, and surface levels, providing an adaptable architecture for targeted mesh processing tasks. We evaluate SAMS's accuracy against existing mesh processing tools. The graph construction results in rich structural representation and has the potential to significantly reduce downstream analytical complexity when detecting vulnerabilities. This paper presents SAMS, its formal graph-theoretic properties, and releases an open-source Python 3.12 implementation on GitHub (https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SAMS-graph-classes/) to facilitate future research in secure additive manufacturing systems software.

title: OmniXRef: A Unified Framework for Multimodal Multi-Reference Video Editing
summary: Creative intent in video editing can be expressed through text instructions (e.g., "remove the people"), image references (e.g., subject appearance), video references (e.g., camera movement), or a combination of the above. We introduce OmniXRef, a unified framework for multimodal multi-reference video editing that allows users to combine variable numbers of text, image, and video references to control diverse attributes of a source video. We first devise a unified input design with a reference-bank interface and introduce $R^2$-RoPE to support generalization to more references. Then our model, OmniXRef-Model, uses a single-stream diffusion transformer to jointly process the source video and multimodal context from an MLLM in an interleaved sequence. To address the scarcity of training data for video-reference editing, we construct OmniXRef-Data using synthesis pipelines for different editing tasks and combinations of references. We use curriculum learning to progressively increase task complexity and resolution. To support systematic evaluation of video as a control modality, we introduce OmniXRef-Bench, a benchmark for video-reference attribute transfer across Camera, Motion, Content, Style, and Visual Effects (VFX). Comprehensive evaluations show that our OmniXRef-Model outperforms task-specific baselines and commercial models.

title: Cross-Person Identity Change Under Source-Coupled Multi-Human Generation: A Controlled UniPortrait Study
summary: Multi-human personalization must account for identity changes in people outside the nominal target of a generative operation. We characterize this behavior in UniPortrait, without introducing a new preservation algorithm. Two sequential studies use 119 accepted two-person baseline scenes and three fixed output seeds, measuring continuous reference-based facial similarity with InsightFace \buffalo. In Study~1, source-coupled single-ID target-only generation (A1) produces negative mean transitions for both the protected person ($-0.567904$) and target ($-0.236904$), indicating broad perturbation rather than established successful repair with collateral loss. In Study~2, native dual-ID generation (A2) yields more positive paired contrasts: protected $+0.512918$ (95\% case-cluster CI $[0.471434,0.550259]$) and target $+0.158853$ ($[0.118903,0.197523]$), across 287 jointly measurable pairs from 111 cases. Shared baseline similarity cancels algebraically in these paired contrasts, leaving a matched POST comparison. Validation designed after the primary result freeze finds directional agreement with an independent identity evaluator and blinded human judgments; within-\buffalo\ nuisance models provide supportive sensitivity evidence. The findings characterize intact native regimes, whose references, routing, adapters, and token counts co-vary. They do not establish component causality, categorical identity preservation, successful localized editing, or generalization beyond the evaluated implementation and measurable cohort.

AI.result: 研究1（单ID目标生成）对受保护者和目标均产生负平均迁移，表明存在广泛扰动；研究2（原生双ID生成）产生更积极的配对对比结果。
AI.conclusion: 研究表明，在UniPortrait中，源耦合的单ID目标生成会导致被保护人物和目标的负面身份迁移，而原生双ID生成则能带来更积极的配对对比结果。
AI.translation: 多人物个性化必须考虑生成操作中非标称目标人物的身份变化。我们在不引入新保持算法的情况下，对UniPortrait中的这种行为进行了表征。两项连续的研究使用了119个接受的双人基线场景和三个固定的输出seed，使用InsightFace \buffalo测量连续的基于参考的面部相似度。在研究1中，源耦合的单ID目标生成（A1）对受保护的人（$-0.567904$）和目标（$-0.236904$）都产生了负的平均迁移，这表明是广泛的扰动，而不是具有附带损失的成功修复。在研究2中，原生双ID生成（A2）产生了更积极的配对对比：在来自111个病例的287个可共同测量的对中，受保护者为 $+0.512918$（95%病例聚类置信区间 $[0.471434, 0.550259]$），目标为 $+0.158853$（$[0.118903, 0.197523]$）。共享的基线相似度在这些配对对比中按代数抵消，留下匹配的POST比较。在主结果冻结后设计的验证发现，与独立的身份评估者和盲法人类判断具有方向性的一致性；\buffalo\内部的干扰模型提供了支持性的敏感性证据。这些发现表征了完好的原生机制，其参考、路由、适配器和token数量协同变化。它们没有确立组件因果关系、类别身份保持、成功的局部编辑，也没有确立超出所评估实现和可测量同类群体的泛化能力。
AI.summary: 本文通过受控研究探讨了UniPortrait在多人物生成中的跨人身份变化，发现单ID生成会导致广泛扰动，而双ID生成则呈现更积极的配对相似度对比。
AI.keywords: 多人物个性化, 身份变化, UniPortrait, 面部相似度, 视觉生成
AI.comments: 本文通过受控实验研究了UniPortrait模型在多人物生成中的跨人身份变化，发现单ID目标生成会导致广泛扰动，而原生双ID生成则表现出更积极的配对对比结果。研究设计严谨，但作者也客观指出了其局限性，如未能确立组件因果关系及泛化能力有限。

title: ElectroCalm: Investigating User Experience and Physiological Responses to Multi-Node Transcutaneous Electrical Stimulation for Stress Modulation
comments: 25 pages, 6 figures, to appear in Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies, Vol. 10, No. 4, December 2026
summary: Transcutaneous Electrical Stimulation (TES) for stress modulation has largely focused on vagus nerve stimulation at the neck, yet two questions remain underexplored: how users experience electrotactile sensations at this sensitive site, and whether electrotactile feedback itself can function as a haptic stress intervention. To investigate this gap, we applied an 8-node TES array to two body sites during a cognitively demanding 2-back task: the neck, a site used in prior vagal TES research for its anatomical proximity to the cervical vagus nerve, and the arm, the most common haptic wearable site, which primarily provides cutaneous electrotactile sensation without vagal access. In a usability study, both sites were rated as comparably comfortable without disrupting task performance, though the same stimulation was interpreted differently across sites. A second study assessing the physiological effects of active versus inactive stimulation under identical electrode attachment revealed that only neck TES produced cortical and autonomic changes consistent with stress modulation, while arm TES did not differ from inactive conditions. These findings suggest that neck TES can be acceptable despite the site's sensitivity, and that both the physiological effects and the sensory experience of TES depend on placement.
comment: 25 pages, 6 figures, to appear in Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies, Vol. 10, No. 4, December 2026

AI.title_translation: ElectroCalm：多节点经皮电刺激用于压力调节的用户体验与生理反应研究
AI.tldr: 本研究通过对比颈部和手臂的多节点经皮电刺激（TES），发现只有颈部TES能有效产生与压力调节相关的皮质和自主神经变化，且两个部位的舒适度均可接受。
AI.motivation: 以往基于颈部迷走神经刺激的经皮电刺激（TES）主要关注压力调节，但对于用户在敏感部位体验电触觉感受的方式，以及电触觉反馈本身能否作为触觉压力干预手段，这两个问题仍未得到充分探讨。
AI.method: 通过两项研究进行调查：1）在进行2-back认知任务时，在颈部和手臂应用8节点TES阵列进行可用性研究；2）进行生理效果评估研究，对比主动刺激与非活动刺激在相同电极附着下的皮质和自主神经变化。
AI.result: 在可用性研究中，两个部位均被评为具有相当的舒适度且不影响任务表现，但刺激在不同部位的解读不同。在生理研究中，只有颈部TES产生了与压力调节一致的皮质和自主神经变化，而手臂TES与非活动条件无异。
AI.conclusion: 本研究表明颈部经皮电刺激（TES）虽然敏感但具有良好的可接受性，且其压力调节的生理效果具有明显的身体部位依赖性（颈部有效而手臂无效）。
AI.translation: 用于压力调节的经皮电刺激（TES）在很大程度上集中于颈部的迷走神经刺激，然而有两个问题仍未得到充分探讨：用户如何体验该敏感部位的电触觉感受，以及电触觉反馈本身是否可以作为一种触觉压力干预手段。为了填补这一空白，我们在认知 demanding 的 2-back 任务期间，将8节点TES阵列应用于两个身体部位：颈部（由于其解剖位置接近颈迷走神经，在以往迷走神经TES研究中使用）和手臂（最常见的触觉可穿戴部位，主要提供没有迷走神经通路的皮肤电触觉感觉）。在可用性研究中，两个部位的舒适度都被评为相当高，且没有干扰任务性能，尽管相同的刺激在不同部位有不同的解读。第二项评估主动刺激与相同电极附着下的非活动刺激的生理效应的研究表明，只有颈部TES产生了与压力调节一致的皮质和自主神经变化，而手臂TES与非活动条件没有差异。这些发现表明，尽管颈部敏感，但颈部TES是可以被接受的，并且TES的生理效应和感觉体验都取决于放置位置。
AI.summary: 该研究调查了多节点经皮电刺激（TES）在颈部和手臂两个部位对压力调节的用户体验与生理反应。研究发现，虽然两个部位的舒适度相近，但只有颈部TES能引起与压力调节相关的皮质和自主神经变化，证明了TES的生理效应和感官体验取决于刺激部位。
AI.keywords: 经皮电刺激, 压力调节, 触觉反馈, 生理反应, 用户体验
AI.comments: 该研究探索了多节点经皮电刺激（TES）在压力调节中的应用，对比了颈部和手臂两个部位的主观体验和生理反应。其创新之处在于将触觉反馈作为压力干预手段，并通过对照实验证明了颈部TES在皮质和自主神经调节上的特异性，为可穿戴压力调节设备提供了有价值的设计见解。

title: Native Geometry vs. Linear Recoverability: How Alignment Changes Platonic Scaling
comments: 10 pages, 6 figures, Accepted to NeurReps 2026 (NeurIPS Workshop on Symmetry and Geometry in Neural Representations), Extended Abstract track
summary: Do larger models learn increasingly similar representations of the same world? The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) predicts that they should, but similar can mean native cosine geometry---nearest-neighbour structure induced by cosine similarity before any learned alignment---or linear recoverability: correspondence revealed by a supervised linear map. Using matched Legacy Survey and Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) embeddings across five model families, we find that Ridge alignment strengthens the relationship between model size and cross-dataset neighbourhood correspondence relative to native cosine geometry. The effect appears in all five families and persists when both representations are reduced to dimension, so it is not simply that wider embeddings give alignment more dimensions to work with. The learned maps remain far from rotations or uniform scaling, and Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) and Block-Sparse Featuriser (BSF) features give no advantage over the same alignment applied to dense embeddings. Model scale thus improves linear recoverability more clearly than native cosine-neighbourhood correspondence, without establishing convergence toward a shared native metric geometry.
comment: 10 pages, 6 figures, Accepted to NeurReps 2026 (NeurIPS Workshop on Symmetry and Geometry in Neural Representations), Extended Abstract track

AI.title_translation: 原生几何与线性可恢复性：对齐如何改变柏拉图式缩放
AI.tldr: 模型规模能更好地提升表示的线性可恢复性，而非原生余弦几何相似性。
AI.motivation: 检验柏拉图式表示假说（PRH），探讨随着模型增大，模型是否学习到越来越相似的世界表示，并厘清“相似”是指原生余弦几何还是线性可恢复性。
AI.method: 使用跨五个模型系列的匹配 Legacy Survey 和 Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) 嵌入，应用 Ridge 对齐、降维控制、稀疏自编码器（SAE）以及块稀疏特征化器（BSF）进行分析。
AI.result: Ridge 对齐增强了模型大小与跨数据集邻域对应性之间的关系（相比于原生余弦几何）；该效应在所有五个模型系列中均出现，且在降维到相同维度后依然存在；学习到的映射远非旋转或均匀缩放，且 SAE 和 BSF 特征没有带来优势。
AI.conclusion: 模型规模更明显地改善了线性可恢复性，而非原生余弦邻域对应性，且并未促成向共享原生度量几何的收敛。
AI.translation: 更大的模型是否会学习到对同一世界越来越相似的表示？柏拉图式表示假说（PRH）预测它们会，但“相似”可以指原生余弦几何（即在任何学习到的对齐之前由余弦相似度诱导的最近邻结构），也可以指线性可恢复性（即通过监督线性映射显示的对应关系）。通过在五个模型系列中使用匹配的 Legacy Survey 和 Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) 嵌入，我们发现，相对于原生余弦几何，Ridge 对齐增强了模型大小与跨数据集邻域对应性之间的关系。这种效现在所有五个模型系列中都有出现，并且当两个表示都降维到相同维度时仍然存在，因此这不仅仅是因为更宽的嵌入为对齐提供了更多的操作维度。学习到的映射远非旋转或均匀缩放，并且稀疏自编码器（SAE）和块稀疏特征化器（BSF）特征并没有比应用于稠密嵌入的相同对齐带来更多优势。因此，模型规模比原生余弦邻域对应性更明显地改善了线性可恢复性，但并没有建立起向共享原生度量几何的收敛。
AI.summary: 论文通过对五个模型系列中匹配嵌入的研究，发现模型规模显著增强了监督线性映射下的线性可恢复性，而原生余弦几何并没有表现出向共享度量几何的收敛，这深化了对“柏拉图式表示假说”中表示相似性内涵的理解。
AI.keywords: 柏拉图式表示假说, 模型规模, 线性可恢复性, 嵌入对齐, 几何结构
AI.comments: 该论文探讨了柏拉图式表示假说（PRH）中关于模型大小与表示相似性的核心问题，通过对比原生余弦几何与线性可恢复性，揭示了模型规模主要增强了线性可恢复性，而未建立向共享原生度量几何的收敛。创新点在于多数据集的匹配嵌入分析以及排除了维度混淆的影响。

title: MedSTP: Preserving Subspace and Transition Evidence for Medical VQA Token Pruning
summary: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) for visual question answering (VQA) often pass long visual-token sequences to the language model, making visual-token pruning attractive but risky for medical images, where answers may depend on localized boundary and texture evidence. We study training free pre-decoding pruning and treat pruning as a subspace stable evidence preservation problem. The retained tokens should remain close to the dominant visual evidence subspace induced by the full token set. To this end, we propose \emph{Subspace-Transition Token Pruning} (\method{}), which estimates each token's spectral support from principal component space and constructs a compact representation subspace. To better reflect medical image structure, \method{} further uses a bounded token-grid transition prior to promote boundary and texture sensitive tokens. We evaluate \method{} on the closed-ended SLAKE and OmniMedVQA benchmarks and on RadImageNet-VQA, which provides both closed-ended and open-ended evaluations, using Lingshu-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B backbones. \method{} delivers consistently strong performance on both the closed-ended and open-ended RadImageNet-VQA evaluations. These results show that \method{} is an effective training free pruning framework for medical domain VQA.

AI.title_translation: MedSTP：为医学VQA Token剪枝保持子空间与过渡证据
AI.tldr: 提出了一种无需训练的医学VQA token剪枝方法MedSTP，通过结合子空间稳定性和过渡先验，在压缩序列长度的同时保护了关键的医学局部证据。
AI.motivation: 医疗视觉语言模型在处理VQA任务时通常会将长视觉token序列传入语言模型，视觉token剪枝虽然具有吸引力，但在医学图像中风险很高，因为答案往往依赖于局部的边界和纹理证据。
AI.method: 提出了Subspace-Transition Token Pruning (MedSTP)方法，通过主成分空间估计每个token的光谱支持来构建紧凑的表示子空间，并利用有界的token-grid过渡先验来促进对边界和纹理敏感的token。
AI.result: 在SLAKE、OmniMedVQA以及包含闭卷和开卷评估的RadImageNet-VQA基准测试（使用Lingshu-7B和Qwen3-VL-8B骨干网络）上，MedSTP均表现出持续且强劲的性能。
AI.conclusion: MedSTP是一种高效、无需训练的医疗领域VQA视觉token剪枝框架，能够在压缩计算成本的同时有效保留关键的医学视觉证据。
AI.translation: 用于视觉问答（VQA）的医疗视觉语言模型（VLMs）通常将长视觉token序列传递给语言模型，这使得视觉token剪枝很有吸引力，但对于医学图像来说风险很高，因为答案可能取决于局部的边界和纹理证据。我们研究了免训练的预解码剪枝，并将剪枝视为一个子空间稳定的证据保持问题。保留的token应保持接近由完整token集诱导的主导视觉证据子空间。为此，我们提出了“子空间-过渡Token剪枝”（MedSTP），它从主成分空间估计每个token的光谱支持，并构建一个紧凑的表示子空间。为了更好地反映医学图像结构，MedSTP进一步使用有界的token-grid过渡先验来提升对边界和纹理敏感的token。我们在闭卷的SLAKE和OmniMedVQA基准测试以及提供闭卷和开卷评估的RadImageNet-VQA上进行了评估，使用了Lingshu-7B和Qwen3-VL-8B骨干网络。MedSTP在闭卷和开卷的RadImageNet-VQA评估中均表现出持续强劲的性能。这些结果表明，MedSTP是一个用于医疗领域VQA的有效、免训练的剪枝框架。
AI.summary: 论文提出了MedSTP（一种针对医学VQA的无需训练的token剪枝框架），通过保持子空间和过渡证据，在压缩视觉token的同时有效保留了医学图像所需的局部边界和纹理细节。
AI.keywords: Medical VQA, Vision-Language Models, Token Pruning, Subspace Stability, Medical Imaging
AI.comments: 该论文针对医疗视觉问答中的视觉token冗余问题，创新性地提出了一种无需训练的子空间与过渡证据保持token剪枝方法（MedSTP）。通过结合主成分空间的光谱支持估计和有界的token网格过渡先验，既保证了全局子空间的稳定性，又兼顾了医学图像中至关重要的局部边界和纹理特征，在多个医学VQA基准测试中表现出色。

title: Refusal Is Not Robustness: Measuring Harmful Reachability in Autoregressive Language Models
summary: LLM safety evaluations via jailbreaking typically index on attack success rate (ASR): whether a generated response violates safeguards. However, ASR only evaluates sampled outputs and provides little information on the underlying generation process. Autoregressive language models define distributions over possible outputs, and a sampled refusal can coexist with substantial probability mass on harmful generation paths. We study this hidden structure through bounded continuation analysis (BCA), which models autoregressive generation as a stochastic process over token prefixes and computes the finite-horizon probability that generation reaches a harmful continuation. BCA constructs a bounded continuation tree, labels terminal continuations with a semantic harm evaluator, and estimates harmful reachability using exact probabilistic model checking. BCA complements ASR by measuring how much harmful behavior remains accessible beneath a sampled safe response. This makes it useful for distinguishing models that look identical under measured ASR values, and allocating red-team effort toward regions of the generation process with greater hidden risk. Across four instruction-tuned LLMs and 100 JailbreakBench behaviors, we show that BCA effectively quantifies hidden harmful behavior and provides a useful signal to guide red teaming.

AI.title_translation: 拒绝并非鲁棒性：衡量自回归语言模型中的有害可达性
AI.tldr: 传统的拒绝响应无法证明大模型的安全性。本文提出了有界延续分析（BCA）方法，通过概率模型检查来衡量模型生成空间中隐藏的有害可达性。
AI.motivation: 现有的基于越狱的大模型安全评估通常依赖于攻击成功率（ASR），它只评估采样的输出，却无法提供关于潜在生成过程的信息，忽视了安全的响应下可能共存的大概率有害生成路径。
AI.method: 提出有界延续分析（BCA）方法，将自回归生成建模为令牌前缀上的随机过程，构建有界延续树，用语义危害评估器标记终端延续，并使用精确概率模型检查估计有害可达性。
AI.result: 对四个指令微调的LLM和100个JailbreakBench行为的实验表明，BCA能够有效地量化隐藏的有害行为，并为指导红队测试提供有用的信号。
AI.conclusion: 通过有界延续分析（BCA），研究证明了拒绝响应并不等同于鲁棒性，BCA能有效量化隐藏的有害行为并指导红队测试。
AI.translation: 通过越狱进行的大模型安全评估通常以攻击成功率（ASR）为指标：即生成的响应是否违反了安全防护栏。然而，ASR仅评估采样的输出，对底层生成过程提供的的信息很少。自回归语言模型定义了可能输出的分布，采样的拒绝可以与有害生成路径上的实质概率质量共存。我们通过有界延续分析（BCA）研究了这种隐藏结构，BCA将自回归生成建模为令牌前缀上的随机过程，并计算生成达到有害延续的有限视野概率。BCA构建有界延续树，用语义危害评估器标记终端延续，并使用精确概率模型检查估计有害可达性。BCA通过衡量在采样的安全响应之下还存在多少有害行为来补充ASR。这使得它在区分在测量的ASR值下看起来相同的模型，以及将红队工作分配给具有更大隐藏风险的生成过程区域方面非常有用。在四个指令微调的大语言模型和100个JailbreakBench行为中，我们表明BCA有效地量化了隐藏的有害行为，并为指导红队测试提供了有用的信号。
AI.summary: 该论文提出了一种名为有界延续分析（BCA）的方法，用于解决传统攻击成功率（ASR）指标无法评估大模型生成过程中隐藏风险的问题。BCA通过精确的概率模型检查计算有害延续的可达概率，能够区分ASR相同但隐藏风险不同的模型，并有效指导红队测试。
AI.keywords: 大模型安全, 越狱攻击, 攻击成功率, 有界延续分析, 概率模型检查
AI.comments: 该论文指出了传统大模型安全评估中攻击成功率（ASR）的局限性，即模型表现出拒答并不代表其生成空间中不存在有害概率。提出的有界延续分析（BCA）方法通过概率模型检查评估隐藏风险，对大模型安全性评估和红队测试具有重要意义。

title: Input- and Feature-Space Correction for Cross-Hospital IHC Grading
comments: 12 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI at Scale for Clinical Impact (ASCI)
summary: Pathology foundation models (FMs) are trained predominantly on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images but are increasingly used as frozen feature extractors for immunohistochemistry (IHC), where cross-hospital differences can impair grading. However, systematic comparisons of correction methods for cross-hospital IHC grading remain limited. To address this gap, we benchmark label-free transformations applied to input images before frozen-FM encoding and to features after frozen-FM encoding using UNI and Virchow2, three IHC markers, and six directed cross-hospital transfers, yielding 12 settings. Among the evaluated input-space methods, our proposed method FIX achieved the largest macro-F1 improvement over no correction, outperforming well-known stain normalization techniques. Among feature-space methods, a simple feature-wise standardization achieved the best improvement over no correction, outperforming CORAL. Under patient-averaged tile-level evaluation, combining FIX with feature-wise standardization improved macro-F1 and quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) by 0.181 and 0.208, respectively, and reduced ordinal error by 0.209 relative to no correction. These results show that input- and feature-space transformations can provide complementary benefits for cross-hospital IHC grading with frozen pathology FMs.

AI.title_translation: 跨医院免疫组化分级的输入与特征空间校正
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种结合输入空间校正（FIX）与特征空间标准化的方法，显著提升了病理基础模型在跨医院免疫组化（IHC）分级中的泛化性能。
AI.motivation: 病理基础模型主要在H&E图像上训练，常被用作免疫组化（IHC）的冻结特征提取器，但跨医院的差异会损害分级性能，且目前缺乏针对跨医院IHC分级校正方法的系统性比较。
AI.method: 对冻结基础模型编码前后的无标签转换方法进行了基准测试。在输入空间提出了FIX方法，并与传统染色归一化技术进行了对比；在特征空间评估了特征级标准化与CORAL方法的性能，并测试了输入与特征空间校正的组合效果。
AI.result: 在输入空间方法中，提出的FIX方法实现了最大的macro-F1提升；在特征空间方法中，简单的特征级标准化表现最佳。结合FIX与特征级标准化可使macro-F1和QWK分别提高0.181和0.208，并降低序数误差。
AI.conclusion: 输入空间与特征空间转换相结合，能够为使用冻结病理基础模型的跨医院IHC分级提供互补的优势，显著提升分级准确性并减少序数误差。
AI.translation: 病理学基础模型（FMs）主要在苏木精和伊红（H&E）图像上训练，但越来越被用作免疫组化（IHC）的冻结特征提取器，而跨医院的差异会损害分级性能。然而，对跨医院IHC分级校正方法的系统性比较仍然有限。为了填补这一空白，我们对在冻结FM编码之前应用于输入图像的无标签转换以及在冻结FM编码之后应用于特征的转换进行了基准测试，使用了UNI和Virchow2、三种IHC标记物以及六个定向跨医院迁移，共产生12种设置。在评估的输入空间方法中，我们提出的方法FIX实现了相对于无校正的最大macro-F1提升，优于众所周知的染色归一化技术。在特征空间方法中，简单的特征级标准化实现了相对于无校正的最佳提升，优于CORAL。在患者平均切片级评估下，将FIX与特征级标准化相结合，相对于无校正，macro-F1和二次加权卡帕（QWK）分别提高了0.181和0.208，序数误差降低了0.209。这些结果表明，输入和特征空间转换可以为使用冻结病理FM的跨医院IHC分级提供互补的益处。
AI.summary: 该论文针对跨医院免疫组化（IHC）分级中由于中心间差异导致病理基础模型性能下降的问题，系统评估并基准测试了输入空间和特征空间中的无标签校正方法。研究表明，提出的输入空间方法FIX与简单的特征级标准化相结合，能够产生互补的优势，显著提升跨医院IHC分级的准确性。
AI.keywords: 免疫组化分级, 跨医院泛化, 病理基础模型, 输入空间校正, 特征标准化
AI.comments: 该论文填补了跨医院免疫组化（IHC）分级中校正方法系统性比较的空白，提出了FIX输入空间校正方法，并结合特征空间标准化，显著提升了病理基础模型在多中心数据上的泛化能力，对计算病理学在临床的实际落地具有重要价值。

title: Between Spoilers and Guesswork: Avoiding Over-Specification in Coding Benchmarks
summary: Benchmarks drive AI progress, but are hampered by task under-specification and over-specification. Task under-specification causes guesswork, where solutions have to make things up, or worse, resort to contamination or reward hacking. Task over-specification causes spoilers, where solutions can bypass some of the harder steps the benchmark was supposed to measure. Since future-looking benchmarks should be difficult, over-specification reduces a benchmark's shelflife of community adoption. Repository-level coding benchmarks have helped the field progress but experience unnecessary churn due to both over- and under-specification. For instance, SWE-bench Pro, FEA-bench, Doc2Feat-bench, and Multi-SWE-bench all tackle under-specification by augmenting task statements with hints derived from ground truth. We show that leaking ground-truth information into the task statement causes over-specification in some of these benchmarks. We experiment with various specification levels, trying to thread the needle between spoilers and guesswork. Based on these results, we recommend techniques for deriving parsimonious hints. We will release our hints so the community can obtain more reliable signals from popular benchmarks.

AI.title_translation: 在剧透与猜测之间：避免编码基准测试中的过规格化
AI.tldr: 通过研究代码基准测试中的规范水平，论文揭示了真实值提示带来的过规格化问题，并提出了推导精简提示以提高评估可靠性的建议。
AI.motivation: 现有的代码基准测试（如SWE-bench Pro等）常因任务欠规格化而引入ground-truth提示，但这导致了过规格化问题（剧透），缩短了基准测试的生命周期。因此，需要研究如何在“剧透”和“猜测”之间找到平衡，避免过规格化。
AI.method: 实验研究了不同的规范级别，分析了将ground-truth信息泄漏到任务描述中所导致的过规格化问题，并提出了推导精简提示（parsimonious hints）的技术。
AI.result: 研究表明，将ground-truth信息泄漏到任务描述中确实会在某些基准测试中引起过规格化，通过适当调整规范级别可以获得更可靠的评估信号。
AI.conclusion: 通过探索不同的规范级别，论文建议使用精简提示的方法来避免代码基准测试中的过规格化和欠规格化，从而提高评估的可靠性。
AI.translation: 基准测试推动了人工智能的进步，但却受到任务欠规格化和过规格化的阻碍。任务欠规格化会导致猜测，迫使解决方案去虚构内容，甚至诉诸数据污染或奖励hacking。任务过规格化则会导致剧透，使解决方案能够绕过基准测试原本旨在衡量的某些更艰难的步骤。由于面向未来的基准测试应该具有难度，过规格化会缩短社区采用基准测试的生命周期。仓库级编码基准测试推动了该领域的进展，但也因过规格化和欠规格化而经历了不必要的动荡。例如，SWE-bench Pro、FEA-bench、Doc2Feat-bench和Multi-SWE-bench都通过用源自ground-truth的提示来扩充任务描述，以解决欠规格化问题。我们表明，将ground-truth信息泄漏到任务描述中会导致其中一些基准测试出现过规格化。我们试验了各种规范级别，试图在剧透和猜测之间找到平衡。基于这些结果，我们推荐了推导精简提示的技术。我们将发布我们的提示，以便社区能够从流行基准测试中获得更可靠的信号。
AI.summary: 该论文研究了代码基准测试中由于任务规范不当引起的“猜测”与“剧透”问题，指出基准测试中引入真实值提示会导致过规格化，并提出了生成精简提示以提升基准测试可靠性的技术。
AI.keywords: 代码基准测试, 过规格化, 欠规格化, 提示词工程, AI评估
AI.comments: 该论文探讨了代码基准测试中任务规范过宽或过窄（过规格化与欠规格化）的关键问题，指出在任务描述中引入ground-truth提示会导致过规格化，并提出了生成精简提示的推荐技术，具有重要的实际指导意义。

title: Shape-Aware Neural Time Fields for Rigid-Body Motion and Manipulation Planning
summary: Rigid-body motion planning is fundamental to robotic transport and manipulation, where both object position and orientation determine whether a body can move through cluttered environments. This coupling makes planning chal- lenging because translation and rotation can be constrained very differently by surrounding geometry. We propose Shape- Aware Neural Time Fields, a physics-informed neural motion planning framework that learns a reusable travel-time, or cost- to-go, representation for rigid-body motion while explicitly accounting for these distinct geometric restrictions. The learned field captures local motion difficulty in translation and rotation and is paired with a sampling-based planner that balances progress toward the goal with the cost of reaching nearby poses. We evaluate the framework across 2D and 3D rigid- body planning tasks and non-prehensile manipulation through object pushing in diverse environments. Results show substantial improvements in planning success and inference efficiency over physics-informed neural planning baselines, while remaining competitive with classical sampling-based planners at significantly lower planning times. Ablation studies further validate the contributions of both the learned representation and the proposed planning strategy.
