AI.title_translation: 广义坐标下的力与运动同时控制
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种基于广义坐标和二次规划的机器人力位混合控制方法，能够完美处理关节级不等式约束并实现精确的接触力控制。
AI.motivation: 传统的力位混合控制通常在操作空间（任务坐标）中进行，难以处理自然表达在广义坐标（关节空间）中的关节极限、避障和防奇异等约束，从而影响控制的可行性。
AI.method: 利用高斯最小约束原理，将力位混合控制问题表述为广义坐标（关节空间）下的二次规划（QP）问题，并可附加不等式约束以保证可行性和安全性。
AI.result: 在MuJoCo中的仿真结果表明，该方法能够同时维持期望的接触力、最小化轨迹跟踪误差，并严格遵守实际的不等式约束，优于传统的操作空间公式。
AI.conclusion: 提出的基于广义坐标和高斯最小约束原理的QP控制方法，能够有效解决传统操作空间控制难以处理关节级约束的问题，实现精确的力控与轨迹跟踪。
AI.translation: 机器人操作臂在执行工作时经常与刚性物体接触，这对其运动施加了物理约束。同时力与运动控制的开发旨在调节与这些约束相称的接触力，同时将运动控制投影到正交的、无约束的方向上。这通常在任务坐标（即操作空间）中进行公式化，然后映射到关节力矩以指挥机器人。然而，大多数机器人控制的约束（如关节极限、防碰撞、避奇异等）自然地在广义坐标（关节空间）中表达。因此，在任务空间中表述控制问题使得保证控制的可行性变得困难。在本文中，高斯最小约束原理被用于将控制问题解决为广义坐标下的二次规划（QP）问题。结果表明，该问题的理论解产生了正确的约束动力学，以实现精确的接触力控制。此外，可以附加不等式约束以确保可行性和安全性。在MuJoCo中进行了仿真结果，并与操作空间公式进行了比较。所提出的方法能够同时保持期望的接触力、最小化轨迹跟踪误差，并遵守实际的不等式约束。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种在广义坐标下进行同时力与运动控制的新方法，利用高斯最小约束原理将控制问题转化为二次规划问题。该方法不仅能保证准确的接触力控制和轨迹跟踪，还能方便地融入关节极限等不等式约束以确保系统安全性。
AI.keywords: 广义坐标, 力位混合控制, 二次规划, 约束动力学, 机器人操作臂
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地将高斯最小约束原理应用于广义坐标下的力位混合控制，转化为二次规划问题，不仅能精确控制接触力，还能方便地处理关节极限等不等式约束，显著提升了机器人在复杂交互任务中的安全性与可行性。

title: Hybrid Cones: Set Representation with Sharp Unions of Minimal Overhead for Nonlinear and Switched Linear Systems
summary:
Reachability analysis and set-based estimation for nonlinear systems require set representations capable of capturing nonconvex geometry. Hybrid Zonotopes (HZs) have recently gained attention because they can encode a union of up to $2^n$ polytopic components. Recent work has further shown that several HZ operations can be made \textit{sharp}, meaning that relaxing the binary variables yields exactly the convex hull of the represented set. However, no known HZ construction provides a sharp union of two convex sets that adds only one binary generator and no further continuous generators or equality constraints to those of the operands. This limitation affects scalability in repeated union operations, ReLU neural-network reachability, and nonlinear propagation methods that cover graph sets by unions of simpler sets.
  This paper identifies a connection between the exact closed-form convex-hull operation for Constrained Convex Generators (CCGs) and the binary-generator structure underlying HZs. We propose Hybrid Cones that can encode up to $2^n$ norm-cone components. Hybrid Cones inherit the logical structure of HZs while allowing richer convex components, including polytopic and norm-based sets. They support sharp unions requiring only one added binary variable and can represent unions and intersections of polytopes and ellipsoids. As a key application, we derive an exact representation of the ReLU graph using only two continuous and one binary generators. Numerical experiments for a localization problem with a nonlinear energy measurement function approximated by a neural network and the stability verification of the closed loop of a double integrator corrupted by a nonlinear disturbance with a saturated Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) controller show substantial reduction in representation size and reduced conservatism in comparison with HZs.

title: FuseRAG: Fusing Structure and Evidence into Inference for Cost-Efficient Graph-based RAG
summary: Graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) exploits relationships among evidence to support multi-hop question answering. However, conveying retrieved graphs through non-unique linear textual contexts to Large Language Models (LLMs) leads to graph-structure degradation and inefficient KV-cache reuse. Meanwhile, graph-structure order optimization is already NP-hard, and the additional KV-cache reuse objective further complicates the search by introducing potentially conflicting orders. To tackle these issues, we propose FuseRAG, a cost-efficient graph-based RAG framework that shifts most retrieved evidence from explicit textual contexts to latent representations. Our main idea is to separate reusable evidence content from query-aware structural interactions in latent space, while retaining only a few explicit facts as semantic anchors. The resulting latent representations are injected into decoder self-attention, where they reshape attention over evidence and thereby influence hidden states and next-token probabilities. This design preserves graph structure through latent interactions, enables evidence reuse beyond exact token-prefix matching. Experiments on three multi-hop question-answering datasets with Llama-3-8B and Qwen3.5-9B show that FuseRAG improves answer quality while achieving up to 2.7x and 2.2x TTFT speedups over the fastest graph-based baseline, respectively.

title: Causal Edit Serialization
comments: 37 pages, including appendices and checklist. Code: https://github.com/Louiii/CES ; data and checkpoints: https://huggingface.co/datasets/lorob/CES
summary: Standard autoregressive language models generate text sequentially, but revision requires referring back to tokens in the input context or those already generated. Causal Edit Serialization (CES) is introduced as a framework for expressing such revisions within the same causal token stream. Special pointer tokens are paired with predicted source addresses, allowing insertion, deletion, replacement, copying and movement to be localized explicitly. A lightweight localization head and dual-index rotary position encoding support both address prediction and conditioning on previously emitted pointers, while retaining a standard causal attention mask. A pretraining procedure combines ordinary language modeling with serialized repairs derived from random corruptions, model-generated edits and repeated text. Across model scales and editing baselines, CES models demonstrate complete applied edits with modestly higher clean-text bits per byte than clean autoregressive models. Supervised and reinforcement-learning post-training provide a grammatical-error-correction proof of concept, producing more beneficial than harmful changes under reference-blind model judging. Correct repair programs also improve subsequent text prediction while the original context and its cached states are retained. CES provides a common interface for generation and localized revision, with potential extensions to iterative refinement and additional pointer-addressed transformations.

title: VISTA: A Multimodal Egocentric Benchmark for Goal-Oriented Perception and Assistance to Blind and Low-Vision Users
comments: Code and dataset are available at https://harvard-ai-and-robotics-lab.github.io/VISTA
summary: Blindness and low vision limit many people's ability to complete daily tasks, motivating AI assistants that provide useful guidance. Yet, existing benchmarks do not adequately test whether vision models can provide effective everyday assistance. In particular, i) existing benchmarks primarily rely on visual and textual inputs, with limited support for other modalities that are increasingly available in egocentric wearable devices such as gaze, inertial measurements, spatial trajectories, and others; and ii) existing evaluations emphasize scene understanding and question answering, with limited coverage of goal-conditioned guidance for blind and low-vision users across everyday tasks. To bridge this gap, we introduce VISTA (Visually Impaired Scene and Task Annotations), a multimodal egocentric benchmark for goal-oriented assistance for blind and low-vision users. VISTA contains $\sim$1,000 egocentric recordings captured with Project Aria glasses; each recording provides synchronized sensor streams, six of which serve as model inputs, and three different types of annotation, covering ten task categories (TC), from object localization to hazard detection. We evaluate 14 representative vision-language models zero-shot on VISTA and design a lightweight multimodal model baseline that integrates all six modalities. Experimental results show that, although existing models can often describe egocentric scenes, they remain limited in generating goal-directed assistive guidance. VISTA thus provides a benchmark for evaluating multimodal models that could improve everyday accessibility.

title: Competitive Online Clustering with Movement Cost
summary:
We study the problem of online clustering with movement cost, which generalizes the fundamental $k$-server problem. At each time step, the algorithm is given a set of points in a metric space and must choose $k$ cluster centers. The cost incurred is the sum of the clustering cost at each time step and the total distance that the centers move over time. Prior work established competitive algorithms for the case $k\in\{1,2\}$ on the line metric with the $k$-median clustering objective; under the $k$-median objective, this problem is also known as facility reallocation. We substantially generalize these results to arbitrary $k$, general metric spaces, and a broad class of clustering objectives.
  Specifically, we consider clustering costs defined as a norm of the distance vector from points to their nearest center, which subsumes the $k$-median, $k$-center, and (square root of) $k$-means objectives, and provide an asymptotically optimal $O(k)$-competitive randomized algorithm against adaptive online adversaries. The algorithm is based on a reduction to the $k$-server problem, establishing a tight connection between the problems. In this reduction, $k$-server requests are generated by Poisson processes, whose arrival rates evolve in continuous time and are driven by a dual representation of the clustering costs. Our method of using Poissonization in this context may also be of independent interest. We demonstrate another use of the idea by deriving similar reductions for batched set chasing problems.
  We also consider a different family of clustering objectives defined as a norm of the vector of cluster radii, which subsumes the sum-$k$-radii and the $k$-center objectives, and give a tight $O(k)$-competitive deterministic algorithm on the line.

title: World Action Critic (WAC) Model: Joint Foresight and Criticism for Policy Learning
summary: World models have shown considerable promise in sequential decision-making by anticipating the consequences of actions and providing predictive foresight for policy learning. However, learning to reason about counterfactual actions remains challenging, since predictive objectives may underemphasize information critical for action evaluation, while unexecuted actions lack observed futures for direct supervision. To address these challenges, we propose the World Action Critic (WAC) Model, which proposes multimodal action candidates and jointly learns candidate-conditioned future prediction and consequence evaluation. In our proposed framework, critic supervision directly shapes intermediate predictive representations during rollout, encouraging them to retain information needed to distinguish action quality. Observed futures supervise prediction for executed actions, while external task-quality targets provide evaluation signals for counterfactual candidates. Through joint optimization, critic signals from these candidates propagate into predictive representations without requiring their observed futures. Our theoretical analysis characterizes critic-guided feature retention and bounds candidate-selection regret. Applied to autonomous driving, WAC achieves 93.4 PDMS on NAVSIM-v1, demonstrating the effectiveness of jointly learning predictive foresight and consequence evaluation.

title: PAC-KD: Pathology-Aware Compositional Knowledge Distillation for Respiratory Sound Classification
summary: Respiratory sound classification distinguishes four categories: Normal, Crackle, Wheeze, and Both (crackle and wheeze). Existing knowledge distillation transfers four-class predictions without explicitly exploiting shared respiratory events, potentially limiting the transfer of event-specific knowledge across individual abnormal classes and the Both class. We propose PAC-KD, a pathology-aware compositional knowledge distillation framework that learns crackle and wheeze presence through two dedicated specialists. Their complementary knowledge is transferred to a unified four-class student, enabling it to effectively capture pathology-specific attributes while preserving class-level discrimination. Furthermore, stable conflict calibration adaptively regulates specialist guidance according to its consistency with classification supervision, mitigating potential supervision conflicts. Experiments on ICBHI and SPRSound achieve Scores of 65.28\% and 89.54\%, respectively, outperforming strong knowledge distillation baselines on both datasets.

title: DefFlow: Goal-Conditioned Deformable Object Manipulation using 3D Point Flows
summary: Manipulating deformable objects toward desired 3D configurations is a fundamental capability for robots operating in unstructured physical environments. However, as the range of possible initial and target configurations grows, goal-conditioned deformable manipulation requires a robot to infer increasingly diverse manipulation behaviors in addition to precise continuous actions. We introduce DefFlow, a framework for goal-conditioned manipulation of deformable objects toward a broad range of 3D configurations. DefFlow learns from demonstrations by jointly predicting the goal-conditioned 3D point flow of the robot and deformable object. We show that this formulation better captures both the manipulation decisions, such as when and where to grasp, release, or re-grasp, and the precise continuous motions required for goal reaching, rather than predicting only the robot flow. Across rope, granular-media, and cloth manipulation settings with diverse initial and target configurations, DefFlow substantially outperforms goal-conditioned action-prediction and robot-flow-only baselines on success rates and goal-distance metrics. We further demonstrate deployment of our framework on a real robot using real point-cloud observations and unseen goal configurations.

title: GRAD: Graph-Structured Antibody Defense for LLM Agents
summary: Memory poisoning and decomposition attacks distribute malicious evidence across the operations of large language model agents. Existing request-level defenses can miss such attacks because they assess individual inputs without connecting earlier information to later actions. Moreover, detectors must adapt as task contexts change, while updates to shared parameters can impair previously learned detection capabilities. To address these challenges, we propose GRAD, which combines graph-based evidence aggregation across operations with an extensible collection of detection experts. Its Semantic-Structural Understanding Module (SSUM) jointly encodes operation text, event attributes, and typed candidate relations in an execution graph to aggregate distributed attack evidence into a graph-level risk score. Its Continual Antibody Adaptation (CAA) adds experts on frozen encoder snapshots and routes inputs by observable graph signatures, acquiring and reusing detection capabilities as tasks arrive. Across Decomp, MCP, and MRT, GRAD achieves AUROCs of 97.19%, 77.59%, and 86.60%, respectively, outperforming Sequential Monitor and locally adapted Agent-Sentry and NeuroTaint. CAA improves final accuracy by 13.08 percentage points over Replay on the cross-dataset task stream. The gain remains 9.05 points with equal family/base-case weights within each task. Its compact drop-in gate performs local model inference in milliseconds without monitoring API calls.

title: Partial-Revelation Panel Forecasting: Predictive Information Gain, Allocation, and Coarsening-Consistent Operators
comments: 27 pages, 2 figures. Code and aggregate result summaries included as ancillary files
summary: We study partial-revelation panel forecasting: given $k$ of $n$ annotator votes on the previous dialogue turn, predict the full count distribution of the next turn's panel. This cross-turn predictive information differs from same-item annotation value. Under any nested revelation mechanism, the population decrement satisfies $V(k)-V(k+1)=I(Y;R_{k+1}\mid X_k)$; a fitted model also contributes adjacent excess-risk differences. Coarsened-completely-at-random (CCAR) masking supplies the exchangeable random-rater interpretation used in our operators. We define coarsening-consistent panel operators with a closed-form Dirichlet-multinomial realization, learned completion, and rater-count transfer. Against per-level lookup, cold-start count negative log-likelihood differences are -0.422/-0.166/-0.014 nats on IEMOCAP/M3ED/EmoWOZ. A held-out rater experiment measures same-item value: first and second additional votes reduce NLL by 0.583/0.221, 0.578/0.184, and 0.180/0.069 nats, respectively. Cross-turn and same-item gains are not interchangeable, and CCAR masks are controlled interventions rather than observed arrival processes. Consistency is auditable but does not guarantee predictive improvement; per-level marginalization can outperform a shared table. Target-free allocation beats uniform only where row-level signal is predictable: at budget one it recovers 83--93% of retrospective feature class headroom on IEMOCAP/M3ED but does not improve EmoWOZ. Gains are modest and corpus-dependent, with several small or null partial-revelation differences. Code and aggregate result artifacts accompany the preprint.

title: Too Emotional to Be Fake? Intra-Utterance Emotion Shifts Expose Failure Modes in Speech Deepfake Detectors
summary: Expressive speech synthesis can now change emotion within a single utterance, yet its impact on deepfake detection remains unclear. We introduce EmoShift, a benchmark comparing emotion-stable (AA) and emotion-changing (AB) speech to examine these effects while accounting for static emotion identity and acoustic confounds. It comprises 7,240 bona fide utterances from four source datasets and 9,720 synthetic utterances generated using four expressive TTS systems. Across seven detectors, we find that emotion changes can make synthetic speech appear more genuine, increasing spoof miss rates by up to 25.3 percentage points on OMG-Emotion at fixed thresholds. Conversely, emotion-changing bona fide speech increases false-alarm rates by up to 24.4 percentage points on IEMOCAP. Further analyses reveal detector-specific sensitivities to emotion trajectories, not fully explained by static emotion identity or splicing artifacts. These findings underscore the importance of emotion dynamics in deepfake detection.

title: The Reliance Hypothesis: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Rises as Language Resource Level Falls
summary: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) faithfulness matters for monitoring, explaining and safely deploying large language models, yet it has been studied mostly in English. Languages differ in level, the amount of text available to learn from, so models know less in lower-resource languages, which may change how much they rely on their reasoning. To our knowledge, we are the first to relate CoT faithfulness to both resource level and task type (knowledge- or reasoning-intensive). On parallel multiple-choice questions from Multilingual Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMMLU) in eight languages, faithfulness rises as resource level falls on knowledge-intensive tasks but not on reasoning-intensive ones, a gap that points the same way across four models and several faithfulness measures. We propose, and find support for, the Reliance Hypothesis: models rely more on their reasoning when they cannot recall the answer, as in lower-resource languages on knowledge-intensive tasks. Model confidence partly explains the effect of resource level, but not the knowledge-reasoning gap. Languages in which models are less confident rely more on reasoning, yet less confident answers within a language do not, a Simpson's paradox. In lower-resource languages, models rely on their reasoning for more answers, not more strongly for each. CoT monitoring may therefore be most informative in lower-resource languages, where it is least often validated.

title: VTrajEmbed: Aligning Text with Video Object Trajectories via Spatiotemporal Embeddings
summary: Fine-grained alignment between text and video object trajectories is a core challenge in multimodal understanding. Existing embedding models excel at global retrieval, yet their single global representation entangles multiple objects and their spatiotemporal dynamics, limiting direct object-level grounding. To address this issue, we propose VTrajEmbed, an embedding model that decomposes a video into object trajectories and aligns each trajectory embedding with text for object-level grounding through retrieval. Our main contributions: (1)Slow-Fast Trajectory Encoding, a dual-branch architecture that establishes trajectory representations by densely sampling low-resolution frames for high-frequency motion cues and sparsely selecting high-resolution frames for scene context, aggregated by a shared LLM backbone; (2)Mask-Guided Contrastive Learning, a training objective built upon these representations that couples an intra-group loss and a batch-level bidirectional loss under a relation mask, excluding unverified relations and preventing confirmed matches from becoming false negatives; (3)Text2Traj-Bench, a trajectory-level text-video benchmark with model-assisted construction and human-verified query--trajectory relations. Experimental results show that VTrajEmbed-5B improves text-to-trajectory and trajectory-to-text R@1 over Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B by 15.48 and 18.05 percentage points, respectively, and achieves 49.48% average R@1 across five global retrieval benchmarks, compared with 42.86% for Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B.

title: Variational and Decomposed method for Mitigating Bimodal Bias in Robust Visual Question Answering
summary: Visual question answering (VQA) models are known to suffer from the bias issue, which refers to overfitting the regularities of frequent patterns. Previously, researchers only consider the language bias. Recently, the multimodal bias is noticed. However, what multimodal bias is remains unclear. In this paper, we investigate the multimodal bias in counting and non-counting questions. We find that they have distinct underlying mechanism, so their biases come from distinct reasons. We provide valuable interpretations of VQA counting mechanism: \textbf{quantity information stems from the magnitude of the multimodal features in specific dimensions.} Thus, counting bias stems from the vision side and propagates to multimodal features through modality fusion, while the non-counting bias stems from primarily language bias and slightly vision bias. Thus, we propose a method to deal with them differently: Variational and Decomposed method for mitigating Bimodal Bias (VDB). It extracts bimodal bias affected by different proportion of vision and language sides. We introduce variational bias models utilizing the principle of Variational Auto-Encoder to learn mainly language bias with slight vision effect, and a bimodal bias model for bimodal bias combining language and vision sides. Extensive experiments on VQACPv2, VQACPv1, and GQAOOD datasets demonstrate the rationality of our claim and the effectiveness of our method. We also provide explanation for the compromised performance on VQAv2.

title: Benchmarking and Enhancing Agentic Causal Discovery
summary: LLM agents can now run causal discovery algorithms on a dataset and report what comes out. Whether they do more than that, such as noticing where an algorithm went wrong and fixing it with further tests, is hard to tell from current benchmarks. Most of them give the variables meaningful names, and an LLM shown only the names of the Tübingen cause-effect pairs already gets 99% of the directions right. With the names removed, the data are usually clean enough that picking a better algorithm than PC closes most of the gap. We introduce Heuresis, a benchmark of anonymous simulated datasets whose mechanisms range from linear Gaussian to heavy-tailed. For each family of datasets it separates what a better existing algorithm can gain from what only a closer look at the data can gain, and it traces every edge an agent changes. Every family leaves a gap that none of the algorithms, the router and the two causal-discovery foundation models we ran can close, so a score above the best chosen algorithm has to come from using the data. We instantiate the benchmark with an agent harness and three LLMs, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and Qwen 3.8 Flash. GPT-6.1 Sol surpasses the best chosen algorithm on all six families, by 14% adjacency F1 on the most difficult one, and Claude Opus 5.5 does so by 7.4% there. A third of the true edges the two agents restore on the two hardest families appear in no algorithm's output. The code and data will be publicly released to facilitate future work.

title: LLM-Guided Dual-Stage Latency Optimization for Closed-Loop 6G V2I Digital Twins
comments: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. 15 pages, 8 figures
summary: Wireless Digital Twins are emerging as a key enabler for predictive network control in 6G Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) systems. However, closed-loop V2I DTs face two dual-stage communication bottlenecks arising from model parameter exchange for V2I DT reconstruction and multi-service V2I traffic delivery after each reconstruction. This paper proposes a closed-loop dual-stage End-to-End (E2E) latency optimization framework that integrates Compressed Personalized Federated Learning with a unified Large-Language-Model-guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning approach. A CPFL-enabled decision-oriented V2I DT is first constructed by jointly predicting Path Loss (PL) and Quality-of-Experience (QoE)-oriented Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Then the framework comprises two temporally coupled but latency-wise distinct optimization stages: Stage I minimizes the joint Uplink (UL) and Downlink (DL) E2E transmission latency of compressed shared backbone's parameters, and Stage II minimizes the service-aware E2E latency of multi-service V2I traffic. As the two stages share aligned agent roles and action space, we develop a unified Semantic-Aware Guidance-Enhanced Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization framework, in which the LLM acts as a training-time semantic planner that provides high-level traffic splitting and power allocation guidance to reduce inefficient exploration, while the MARL agents execute feasible low-level actions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables efficient V2I DT reconstruction and significantly reduces both E2E latency for DT reconstruction and multi-service V2I traffic. The proposed SAGE-MAPPO supports cross-stage policy reuse by sequentially solving the two stages within each DT update cycle, which accelerates convergence relative to the existing baselines and facilitates timely DT updates in dynamic V2I scenarios.

title: Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Policy Improvement via Flow-Reversed Action Anchors
summary: Generalist robot policies offer strong behavioral priors, but achieving deployment-level reliability and throughput remains difficult. Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve these policies, yet its effectiveness is constrained by the cost of online interaction. Existing methods adapt frozen flow-matching policies by treating noise space as a continuous action space. We show that this behaviorally unstructured space makes exploration inefficient, often preventing these methods from extracting meaningful learning signals on challenging tasks. We introduce AnchorQ, which enables coarse-to-fine policy improvement through a structured, refinable latent action representation. At each decision step, AnchorQ uses flow reversal to map reference behaviors to state-conditioned latent anchors, samples local particles around those anchors, and applies value-guided sampling to explore promising refinements. Our analysis shows that anchors reduce identification complexity at the cost of support bias; particle refinement trades this bias against action-class complexity; and critic accuracy determines the reliability of KL-regularized, value-guided selection. Across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, AnchorQ outperforms state-of-the-art post-training baselines in sample efficiency, delivering a 37% improvement in real-world success rate and 97% higher simulated task throughput under the same interaction budget. Additional visualizations are available on our website https://anchorq-rl.com/.

AI.tldr: AnchorQ通过引入结构化的、可精炼的潜在动作表示，解决了现有RL方法在策略改进中探索效率低下的问题。它利用流反转将参考行为映射到状态条件潜在锚点，并通过基于值的采样来优化这些锚点，从而在模拟和现实世界的机器人操作任务中显著提高了样本效率和任务成功率。
AI.motivation: 现有的强化学习方法在改进通用机器人策略时，由于在线交互成本高，探索效率低下，难以在具有挑战性的任务中提取有效的学习信号。
AI.method: AnchorQ利用流反转将参考行为映射到状态条件潜在锚点，然后对锚点附近的粒子进行采样，并通过基于值的采样来探索有希望的改进方向，实现粗粒度到细粒度的策略改进。
AI.result: AnchorQ在模拟和现实世界的机器人操作任务中，相比于最先进的训练后基线方法，在样本效率方面表现更优，真实世界成功率提高了37%，模拟任务吞吐量提高了97%，同时保持了相同的交互预算。
AI.conclusion: AnchorQ通过引入结构化的潜在动作表示和有效的采样策略，显著提高了策略改进的样本效率和性能，克服了现有方法的局限性。
AI.translation: 通用机器人策略提供了强大的行为先验，但实现部署级别的可靠性和吞吐量仍然很困难。强化学习（RL）可以改进这些策略，但其有效性受到在线交互成本的限制。现有方法通过将噪声空间视为连续动作空间来调整冻结的流匹配策略。我们表明，这种行为上无结构的 त्यामुळे探索效率低下，常常导致这些方法在具有挑战性的任务上无法提取有意义的学习信号。我们引入了AnchorQ，它通过一个结构化的、可精炼的潜在动作表示来实现粗粒度到细粒度的策略改进。在每个决策步骤，AnchorQ利用流反转将参考行为映射到状态条件潜在锚点，在锚点周围采样局部粒子，并应用基于值指导的采样来探索有希望的精炼。我们的分析表明，锚点以支持偏差为代价降低了识别复杂度；粒子精炼用该偏差换取动作类别复杂度；批评家准确性决定了KL正则化、基于值指导的选择的可靠性。在模拟和现实世界的操纵任务中，AnchorQ在样本效率方面优于最先进的训练后基线方法，在相同的交互预算下，真实世界的成功率提高了37%，模拟任务吞吐量提高了97%。我们网站 https://anchorq-rl.com/ 上提供了额外的可视化。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了一种名为AnchorQ的强化学习方法，用于改进通用机器人策略。与现有方法将噪声空间视为连续动作空间不同，AnchorQ引入了一种结构化的、可精炼的潜在动作表示。通过流反转技术将参考行为映射到状态条件潜在锚点，并结合基于值指导的采样策略，AnchorQ能够更有效地进行探索和策略改进。实验结果表明，AnchorQ在样本效率、真实世界成功率和模拟任务吞吐量方面均显著优于现有方法。
AI.keywords: 强化学习, 策略改进, 潜在动作表示, 流反转, 样本效率
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一种新颖的AnchorQ方法，通过结构化的潜在动作表示和有效的采样策略解决了强化学习中策略改进的样本效率问题，并在机器人操作任务中取得了显著的性能提升。该方法在理论分析和实验验证上都具有一定的说服力，但其在处理更复杂、高维状态空间或更广泛任务类型时的泛化能力仍有待进一步验证。

title: Clinically Informed Acoustic-Aware Attribute Modeling for Respiratory Sound Classification
summary: Automated respiratory sound classification (RSC) aims to identify normal and adventitious respiratory sounds, such as crackles and wheezes. Most existing methods formulate RSC as a flat four-class classification problem over norma, crackle, wheeze and both. However, unlike conventional classification tasks with semantically independent and mutually exclusive categories, the commonly used four-class RSC labels have a compositional structure and can be represented by two clinically meaningful sound attributes: crackle presence and wheeze presence. Existing flat classifiers do not explicitly exploit this structure, which may increase the learning burden by treating the four labels as independent targets. Meanwhile, crackles and wheezes exhibit distinct temporal characteristics, with sparse transient crackle events and sustained continuous wheeze patterns, making a single temporal aggregation strategy less suitable for modeling different adventitious sound evidence. To address these limitations, we propose an Acoustic-Aware Asymmetric Framework (AAAF) for RSC. AAAF reformulates four-class recognition as two sound-attribute detection tasks and recovers the final category through logical composition during inference. Built upon a pretrained BEATs encoder, AAAF employs branch-specific multi-layer fusion and asymmetric temporal aggregation to capture localized crackle evidence and sustained wheeze patterns. Auxiliary normal--abnormal supervision and a batch-adaptive dynamic loss are further introduced to improve global discrimination and robustness under imbalanced labels. Experiments on ICBHI and SPRSound demonstrate that AAAF improves overall RSC performance and generalizes across datasets, achieving a state-of-the-art four-class Score of 65.30% on ICBHI.

AI.title_translation: 基于临床先验声学感知属性建模的呼吸音分类
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种名为AAAF的新框架，将呼吸音四分类任务转化为两个临床属性检测任务，并采用非对称时间聚合策略，在ICBHI数据集上取得了SOTA性能。
AI.motivation: 现有的呼吸音分类方法将其视为扁平的四分类问题，忽视了标签具有的组合结构（爆裂音和哮鸣音属性），增加了学习负担；同时爆裂音和哮鸣音具有不同的时间特征，单一的时间聚合策略不适合建模不同的异常声音证据。
AI.method: 提出声学-感知非对称框架（AAAF），基于预训练的BEATs编码器，将四分类任务重构为两个声学属性检测任务（爆裂音和哮鸣音），采用分支特定的多层融合和非对称时间聚合，并引入辅助正态-异常监督和批自适应动态损失。
AI.result: 在ICBHI和SPRSound数据集上的实验表明，AAAF提高了整体呼吸音分类性能并具有良好的跨数据集泛化能力，在ICBHI上实现了65.30%的最先进的四分类得分。
AI.conclusion: 论文提出的AAAF框架通过声学属性建模、非对称时间聚合及辅助监督，有效解决了传统呼吸音分类中标签组合结构未被利用和时序特征差异大的问题，在ICBHI和SPRSound数据集上取得了最先进的性能。
AI.translation: 自动化呼吸音分类（RSC）旨在识别正常和附加呼吸音，如爆裂音和哮鸣音。大多数现有方法将RSC构想为针对正常、爆裂音、哮鸣音和两者的扁平四分类问题。然而，与具有语义独立且互斥类别的常规分类任务不同，常用的四分类RSC标签具有组合结构，可以用两个具有临床意义的声音属性来表示：爆裂音存在与哮鸣音存在。现有的扁平分类器没有显式利用这一结构，将四个标签视为独立目标可能会增加学习负担。同时，爆裂音和哮鸣音表现出不同的时间特征，稀疏的瞬态爆裂音事件与持续的连续哮鸣音模式使得单一的时间聚合策略不太适合建模不同的附加声音证据。为了解决这些局限性，我们提出了一种用于RSC的声学-感知非对称框架（AAAF）。AAAF将四分类识别重新表达为两个声音属性检测任务，并在推理过程中通过逻辑组合恢复最终类别。建立在预训练的BEATs编码器之上，AAAF采用分支特定的多层融合和非对称时间聚合来捕获局部爆裂音证据和持续哮鸣音模式。进一步引入了辅助正常-异常监督和批自适应动态损失，以提高标签不平衡下的全局辨别力和鲁棒性。在ICBHI和SPRSound上的实验表明，AAAF提高了整体RSC性能并跨数据集泛化，在ICBHI上实现了65.30%的最先进的四分类得分。
AI.summary: 该论文针对呼吸音分类中标签结构未被充分利用及不同声音时序特征差异的问题，提出了一种声学-感知非对称框架（AAAF）。该方法将四分类转化为两个声学属性检测任务，并利用分支特定多层融合、非对称时间聚合以及辅助监督，在公开数据集上取得了领先的性能。
AI.keywords: Respiratory sound classification, Sound-attribute detection, Asymmetric temporal aggregation, Clinical prior, BEATs encoder
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地将传统的四分类呼吸音识别任务重构为两个声学属性检测任务，并结合了临床先验知识和非对称的时间聚合策略，显著提升了分类性能并展现了良好的泛化能力。

title: Uncertainty-Aware Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Tree Search
summary: Tree search enhances multi-step reasoning in large language models (LLMs), yet prevailing methods expand every step with a fixed budget, irrespective of the marginal utility of expansion. We first show, across existing search algorithms, that continuations sampled from a shared intermediate state are largely duplicates and collapse to a few distinct answers. Critically, we find that the semantic dispersion of sibling actions predicts the redundancy of their downstream continuations, permitting a subtree's budget to be fixed before expansion. An information-theoretic analysis motivates this: treating the per-step budget as the Monte Carlo sample size for estimating a step's residual answer entropy, we derive a sufficient budget that shrinks with sibling dispersion. We accordingly propose $\textbf{Uncertainty-Aware Allocation}$ (UAA), a training-free framework that decouples value from uncertainty: values determine which candidates are promising, while uncertainty, estimated from sibling dispersion at no additional model cost, determines how many merit expansion, via uncertainty-aware pruning and uncertainty-aware budgeting. Across mathematical reasoning, logical reasoning, and planning benchmarks, UAA reduces token usage by up to $90\%$ and latency by up to $9\times$ at comparable accuracy, generalizing across four tree search algorithms and both open- and closed-source LLMs.

AI.title_translation: 面向高效LLM树搜索的不确定性感知预算分配
AI.tldr: 通过利用同级动作的语义离散度动态调整LLM树搜索的计算预算，UAA框架在保持准确率的同时，大幅减少了Token消耗（高达90%）和延迟（高达9倍）。
AI.motivation: 现有的LLM树 search 方法在每个步骤中使用固定预算扩展，忽略了边际效用，且从共享中间状态采样的延续往往高度重复。为了解决计算资源浪费问题，需要根据不确定性动态分配预算。
AI.method: 提出不确定性感知分配（UAA）框架。利用同级动作的语义离散度预测下游延续的冗余度，将其作为估计残余答案熵的蒙特卡洛样本大小，通过不确定性感知剪枝和预算分配来确定扩展数量。
AI.result: 在数学推理、逻辑推理和规划基准测试中，在保持可比准确率的同时，UAA将Token使用量减少了高达90%，延迟提高了高达9倍，并泛化于四种树 search 算法以及开源和闭源LLM。
AI.conclusion: UAA框架通过解耦价值与不确定性，根据语义离散度动态分配树搜索预算，显著提升了LLM多步推理的效率，且具有极强的通用性。
AI.translation: 树搜索增强了大语言模型（LLM）的多步推理能力，然而现有方法在每一步都使用固定预算进行扩展，而不考虑扩展的边际效用。我们首先表明，在现有的搜索算法中，从共享中间状态采样的延续很大程度上是重复的，并且会收敛到几个不同的答案。至关重要的是，我们发现同级动作的语义离散度可以预测其下游延续的冗余度，从而允许在扩展之前确定子树的预算。信息论分析激发了这一灵感：将每步预算视为估计步骤残余答案熵的蒙特卡洛样本大小，我们推导出了一个随同级离散度缩小的充足预算。因此，我们提出了“不确定性感知分配”（UAA）这一无需训练的框架，它将价值与不确定性解耦：价值决定了哪些候选者是有前途的，而通过不确定性感知剪枝和不确定性感知预算分配，由模型零额外成本的同级离散度估计出的不确定性决定了多少候选者值得扩展。在数学推理、逻辑推理和规划基准测试中，UAA在保持可比准确率的同时，将Token使用量减少了高达90%，延迟降低了高达9倍，并可泛化到四种树搜索算法以及开源和闭源LLM。
AI.summary: 该论文提出了不确定性感知分配（UAA）框架，这是一种无需训练的方法，它利用同级动作的语义离散度来动态分配LLM树搜索中的计算预算，从而在保持推理准确率的同时大幅降低了Token消耗与延迟。
AI.keywords: 大语言模型, 树搜索, 预算分配, 不确定性感知, 多步推理
AI.comments: 该论文针对大语言模型树搜索中计算资源浪费的问题，创新性地利用同级动作的语义离散度（semantic dispersion）来预测下游延续的冗余度，并结合信息论提出了无训练的预算分配框架。这在保持准确率的同时大幅减少了Token消耗和延迟，具有很高的实用价值和理论支撑。

title: Evo-B&B: Behavior-Aware LLM-Guided Joint Evolution of Branching and Node Selection Policies for MILP
summary: In branch-and-bound for Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP), branching and node selection are two critical and tightly coupled decisions, yet most existing learning-based approaches focus on optimizing them separately. We propose Evo-B&B, an LLM-guided evolutionary framework that jointly evolves executable branching and node selection policies using end-to-end SCIP solving feedback. To improve search efficiency and reduce redundant evaluations of behaviorally similar policies, Evo-B&B introduces a behavior-aware multi-island evolutionary mechanism. It measures policy similarity from branching and node-selection behaviors on a fixed set of B&B decision states and uses this similarity to preserve population diversity. We evaluate Evo-B&B on four standard MILP benchmarks across multiple instance scales. Experimental results show that Evo-B&B achieves competitive solving performance and generalizes well to larger-scale instances, while ablation studies further demonstrate the effectiveness of joint evolution and behavior-aware diversity management.

AI.title_translation: Evo-B&B：面向混合整数线性规划的基于行为感知大语言模型引导的分支与节点选择策略联合演化
AI.tldr: 提出了一种名为Evo-B&B的LLM引导演化框架，用于联合优化MILP中的分支和节点选择策略，显著提升了求解性能与泛化能力。
AI.motivation: 在混合整数线性规划（MILP）的分支定界法中，分支和节点 selection 是两个关键且紧密耦合的决策，然而现有的学习方法大多将它们分开优化，缺乏联合优化与高效的策略搜索机制。
AI.method: 提出Evo-B&B框架，利用大语言模型引导、基于端到端SCIP求解反馈的行为感知多岛演化机制，联合演化可执行的分支和节点选择策略，并通过策略行为相似性来维持种群多样性。
AI.result: 在四个标准MILP基准测试及多种实例规模上的实验表明，Evo-B&B取得了极具竞争力的求解性能，并能够很好地泛化到更大规模的实例中。
AI.conclusion: Evo-B&B通过LLM引导的行为感知联合演化框架，有效解决了MILP中分支与节点选择策略的分离优化问题，在多个标准基准测试中展现出优异的求解性能与可扩展性。
AI.translation: 在混合整数线性规划（MILP）的分支定界中，分支和节点选择是两个关键且紧密耦合的决策，然而大多数现有的基于学习的方法都集中于将它们分别优化。我们提出了 Evo-B&B，一个由大语言模型（LLM）引导的演化框架，它利用端到端的 SCIP 求解反馈来联合演化可执行的分支和节点选择策略。为了提高搜索效率并减少对行为相似策略的冗余评估，Evo-B&B 引入了一种行为感知的多岛演化机制。它通过在一组固定的 B&B 决策状态上的分支和节点选择行为来衡量策略相似性，并利用这种相似性来保持种群多样性。我们在多个实例规模的四个标准 MILP 基准测试上评估了 Evo-B&B。实验结果表明，Evo-B&B 实现了具有竞争力的求解性能，并能很好地泛化到更大规模的实例，同时消融实验进一步证明了联合演化和行为感知多样性管理的有效性。
AI.summary: 本文提出了Evo-B&B，一个由大语言模型引导的演化框架，用于联合优化MILP中的分支和节点选择策略。通过引入行为感知的多岛演化机制来保持种群多样性并减少冗余评估，该方法在多个基准测试中展现了出色的求解性能与泛化能力。
AI.keywords: Mixed-Integer Linear Programming, Branch-and-Bound, Large Language Models, Evolutionary Algorithms, Policy Optimization
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地将大语言模型（LLM）与演化算法结合，用于混合整数线性规划（MILP）中高度耦合的分支与节点选择策略的联合优化。其提出的行为感知多岛演化机制有效避免了冗余评估并维持了种群多样性，展示了良好的泛化能力。

title: Understanding KV Residency in Production-Scale Agentic LLM Workloads
summary: Agentic large language model (LLM) applications turn one user request into a sequence of model and tool calls over a growing context. Retaining this context's key-value (KV) state in GPU memory lets later calls reuse it instead of recomputing it, but at fleet scale this needs substantial memory. We characterize four production Microsoft M365 workload traces (Deep Research, Enterprise Assistant, Coding Agent and Enterprise Chat) spanning more than 121 million model calls. In Deep Research, the application issues 89% of model calls and the median context grows from about 10K to 68K tokens by the 30th call. About 80% of context tokens are served from the prefix cache. With the public Llama-2-70B KV layout standing in for confidential models, one 99th-percentile Deep Research session exceeds the 80 GB HBM of an NVIDIA H100, and holding all live sessions at their peak needs an estimated 501.8 TB of HBM, although inference occupies only 5.6% of that retention time. Trace-driven replay shows that a one-hour idle cap cuts this ceiling by 3.6x while raising the share of calls that recompute context only from 4.07% to 4.53%. Under tighter budgets, eviction alone is insufficient: at one tenth of the busiest hour's demand, LRU eviction makes 63% of Deep Research calls recompute and clairvoyant furthest-next-use 31%, whereas multi-resolution retention (MRR), which demotes the LRU session's KV state to int4, lowers this to 13.6%. Placement imposes a separate limit: when the next call reaches a different deployment, cached-context reuse drops from 89% to 29%, and treating KV state as deployment-local raises the recompute floor under unlimited memory from 5.4% to 20.2%. These findings motivate retention that changes the representation of KV state, together with deployment-aware routing or migration. We plan to release AgenticTraceSim, a parametric trace generator, and a residency replay framework.

AI.title_translation: 理解生产规模Agentic LLM工作负载中的KV驻留
AI.tldr: 本文深入研究了大规模生产级Agentic LLM工作负载中的KV缓存驻留特征，指出Agent应用面临巨大的KV内存压力，并证明了多分辨率保留（MRR）和部署感知路由是优化KV缓存重用的关键手段。
AI.motivation: 智能体（Agentic）LLM应用将单个用户请求转化为一系列模型和工具调用，导致上下文不断增长。在集群规模下，在GPU内存中保留这些上下文的KV状态需要消耗巨大的内存，因此需要理解生产级Agentic LLM工作负载中的KV驻留特征并寻找优化方案。
AI.method: 通过对微软M365四个生产级工作负载（包含超1.21亿次模型调用）进行特征刻画和基于追踪的重放模拟（Trace-driven replay），评估了不同闲置上限、驱逐策略（如LRU、MRR）以及放置策略对KV缓存重用率和内存占用的影响。
AI.result: 研究发现，一个99百分位的Deep Research会话的KV状态会超过单个H100的80GB内存；一小时的闲置上限可将内存峰值需求降低3.6倍且几乎不增加重计算；多分辨率保留（MRR）策略在资源紧张时能将重计算比例降至13.6%；此外，跨部署的路由会使缓存重用率从89%大幅降至29%。
AI.conclusion: 大规模Agent应用中的KV缓存管理面临巨大的内存压力和路由挑战。单纯依靠驱逐策略会导致严重的重计算，而结合低精度量化（如MRR）和部署感知路由/迁移是解决该瓶颈的有效途径。
AI.translation: 智能体大语言模型（LLM）应用将一个用户请求转化为在不断增长的上下文中进行的一系列模型和工具调用。在GPU内存中保留此上下文的键值（KV）状态允许后续调用重用它而不是重新计算，但这在集群规模下需要大量的内存。我们对涵盖超过1.21亿次模型调用的四个生产级微软M365工作负载追踪（Deep Research、企业助手、编码智能体和企业聊天）进行了特征分析。在Deep Research中，应用发起了89%的模型调用，到第30次调用时，中位数上下文从约10K增加到68K个token。约80%的上下文token是从前缀缓存中提供的。以公开的Llama-2-70B KV布局代表机密模型，单个99百分位的Deep Research会话超出了NVIDIA H100的80 GB HBM，保持所有活跃会话处于峰值状态估计需要501.8 TB的HBM，尽管推理仅占该保留时间的5.6%。追踪驱动的重放表明，一小时的闲置上限将此上限削减了3.6倍，同时将仅重新计算上下文的调用比例从4.07%提高到4.53%。在更紧缩的预算下，仅靠驱逐是不够的：在最繁忙一小时需求的十分之一时，LRU驱逐导致63%的Deep Research调用重新计算，而先知式最远下一次使用（clairvoyant furthest-next-use）导致31%，相比之下，将LRU会话的KV状态降级为int4的多分辨率保留（MRR）将其降低到13.6%。放置施加了一个单独的限制：当下次调用到达不同的部署时，缓存上下文的重用率从89%下降到29%，并且将KV状态视为部署本地会在内存无限的情况下将重计算底线从5.4%提高到20.2%。这些发现促成了改变KV状态表示的保留方法，以及部署感知的路由或迁移。我们计划发布AgenticTraceSim（一个参数化追踪生成器）和驻留重放框架。
AI.summary: 该论文通过分析微软四个生产级Agentic LLM工作负载的超1.21亿次模型调用，揭示了这类应用中KV缓存内存需求巨大且上下文增长迅速的特点。研究表明，采用多分辨率保留（MRR）策略及部署感知的路由或迁移，可以有效解决内存受限与上下文重计算之间的矛盾。
AI.keywords: Agentic LLM, KV Cache, Memory Residency, Production Workloads, Multi-resolution Retention
AI.comments: 该论文首次在大规模生产级Agentic LLM工作负载下深入剖析了KV缓存的驻留特征，揭示了Agent应用中上下文急剧增长及高内存占用的挑战，并提出了多分辨率保留（MRR）等缓解策略，对未来大模型推理基础设施的设计具有重要指导意义。

title: The Source of Data Value: Consumer Disclosure, Access Design, and Platform Monetization
summary: Digital marketplaces increasingly earn revenue from transaction commissions and seller-facing data services. Sellers may purchase data to increase revenue or avoid competing with an informed rival. We examine how consumer disclosure rights shape these motives and the platform's incentive to provide data. We develop a game-theoretic model of a commissioned platform, two differentiated sellers, and privacy-sensitive consumers. Data generates value through bilateral sales-revenue gains and competition threats arising from asymmetric access. Under mandatory collection, the platform can monetize defensive adoption, even when bilateral personalization reduces seller revenue. Under voluntary disclosure, anonymous purchasing and strictly positive privacy costs make unilateral disclosure unattractive in the baseline. Exclusive access thus yields no usable information, restores sellers' no-data rejection payoffs, and eliminates defensive fees. Profitable provision therefore requires nonnegative bilateral revenue gains. Under full fee extraction, sellers retain their no-data net profits. This revenue alignment does not guarantee welfare gains: additional transactions may benefit consumers, whereas segmentation in an already covered market can raise anonymous prices and reduce welfare. Capping anonymous offers at their no-data benchmark protects individual consumers and limits positive-mass provision to the transaction-creation region. Extensions consider access choice, heterogeneous privacy costs, imperfect identification, and limited contractual credibility. Platforms should evaluate data services based on both bilateral-use and seller-rejection outcomes, and sellers should distinguish revenue-enhancing from defensive investments. Regulators should distinguish equal-access rules from effective consumer control and monitor pricing in anonymous channels.
